articles.title: F5 Patches Critical NGINX2Root Flaws as PoC Exploits Go Public
articles.summary:
F5 on Wednesday announced patches for 22 vulnerabilities, including five critical-severity NGINX bugs that could lead to unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE).
Referred to as NGINX2Root, the five issues are tracked as CVE-2026-113425, CVE-2026-121810, CVE-2026-123007, CVE-2026-123633, and CVE-2026-123634 (CVSS score of 9.2).
CVE-2026-113425 affects NGINX instances configured as mail proxy servers and can be exploited via specially crafted mail sessions. CVE-2026-121810 can be exploited on servers that use HTTP/3 to trigger a use-after-free in the NGINX worker process.
CVE-2026-123634 impacts servers configured as proxies and can be triggered if the proxied server name includes variables, and a subrequest to a location resolving that server name is received from a Server Side Includes (SSI) or mirror directive.
CVE-2026-123007 and CVE-2026-123633 require HTTP/2 to be enabled on an affected server. Successful exploitation of the former leads to a buffer overflow, while the latter triggers a use-after-free in the worker process.
The two issues were independently reported by Ikotas Labs, Metnir, Rapid7, Wiz, and Xint. They explain that attackers could exploit them to run commands with the privileges of the nginx worker process and fully compromise the server.
“Our testing of CVE-2026-123007 demonstrated code execution on NGINX serving ordinary static files, without a backend application or third-party modules,” Wiz explains, noting that the flaw affects all NGINX iterations…

articles.title: Al menos el 10% de la población mundial sufre un uso problemático de internet: “Hay que priorizar la salud pública frente a la industria”
articles.summary: Una mujer consulta Instagram en su teléfono móvil. Existe un término. Se inventó durante la década de los noventa y se llama “adicción a internet”. Pero ya no es suficiente, se ha quedado obsoleto. Por ello, la Comisión de la prestigiosa revista The Lancet Psychiatry ha decidido emplear otro: “Uso problemático de internet” (PUI, en inglés). Y las razones no son muy halagüeñas. En un documento publicado este jueves , la Comisión estima que el PUI afecta al menos al 10% de la población mundial. Una situación que abarca desde los trastornos por apuestas y videojuegos en línea , pasando por el consumo adictivo del porno , hasta llegar a conductas “emergentes” como la cibercondría —los hipocondriacos de siempre, solo que ahora potenciados por las infinitas y aterradoras posibilidades de la red—. articles.title: AI can write code, but knowing what to build still matters
articles.summary:
AI can write code, but knowing what to build still matters
At TechSparks 2026, Srinivas Chamarthy of Diligent India, Madhusudan N. Murthy of EY GDS, and Arun Kalyanaraman of Target discussed why domain expertise, engineering skills, and human judgement remain important as AI makes software development more accessible.
AI is making it easier to build software. Product managers, designers, and domain experts can now turn ideas into prototypes without necessarily knowing how to code. But turning those prototypes into reliable products that solve real problems remains a challenge.
At TechSparks 2026, Srinivas Chamarthy, Senior Vice President of Engineering, Site Lead and Country Head at Diligent India; Madhusudan N. Murthy, Digital Engineering and Tech Strategy Leader at EY GDS; and Arun Kalyanaraman, VP of Engineering at Target in India, discussed these changes during a panel titled ‘From Who Can Code to Who Can Build’.
The discussion was moderated by Chhavi Mahajan, Chief Content Officer at YourStory.
From prototypes to production
AI-assisted development allows business teams to test ideas, demonstrate concepts, and gather feedback much earlier. However, a prototype that shows an idea can work is not necessarily ready for production. Applications still need to meet security, scalability, and reliability requirements.

articles.title: Some creators are skeptical of Instagram’s new affiliate program
articles.summary:
For years, influencers have come up with workarounds on social media to figure out how to share affiliate links with followers. A new integration between Instagram and Amazon was announced earlier this month as a way to make it easier for influencers to make money from affiliate links — but some content creators are suspicious about who really benefits.
Some creators are skeptical of Instagram’s new affiliate program
Influencers are now able to link their Amazon and Instagram accounts to promote products. Some are concerned about what they’re opting in to.
The new integration allows creators to connect their Instagram and Amazon accounts and automatically tag products with their affiliate links, from which they earn a commission when followers make purchases. Influencers will be able to embed up to 30 product links in a Reel or 20 in a feed post, but a permissions setting has led to concerns about what creators are actually agreeing to.
In connecting an Amazon account, creators must agree to allow the retailer and its brand sellers to create ads from “any public content” that includes a related affiliate link. Influencers must also agree to acknowledge that brands can edit their content and use their “testimonial, caption or media” for ads.

articles.title: Internet traffic and attacks during the 2026 U.S. midterm elections
articles.summary:
Internet traffic and attacks during the 2026 U.S. midterm elections
Visitors to government election websites surged 363% on November 3, the date of the 2026 midterm elections in the United States. Across Cloudflare's election protection programs, we also detected a significant shift in the types and timing of cyberattacks throughout 2026.
Unlike what we saw in other recent elections, attackers focused on gaining access to internal systems and data, rather than knocking websites offline. Government election websites faced website vulnerability attempts 180 times more often than denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks, and at roughly ten times the rate of Cloudflare's broader customer base. We also found evidence of at least one attempt to exploit a recently disclosed critical PHP vulnerability on a state government voting website in the Western United States.
These attacks peaked in late October, several weeks before the election. Vulnerability exploit attempts climbed steadily throughout 2026: from 200,000 per day in January, to 2 million per day in October. However, on Election Day in the U.S., Cloudflare detected no escalation in attack volume and zero major DDoS incidents across protected election sites, marking a sharp contrast to other recent elections, such as in Moldova last year.
Our data regarding cyberattacks on election institutions came from organizations participating in Cloudflare's free cybersecurity programs: the Athenian Project, Cloudflare for Campaigns, and Projec…

articles.title: November 2026 Top500 New Systems Are Few and Far Between
articles.summary:
The November 2026 TOP500 list has only 28 new systems, the lowest count in our tracking series going back to June 2018. This dramatic slowdown from previous editions marks a significant shift in how often the list turns over with fresh hardware.
New System Counts Hit a Series Low
Just as a quick note, the official Top500 post says there were 27 new systems, but when we filtered the list on First Appearance 68 (with 68 being the November 2026 list), we got 28 new systems. We will use these new systems for our analysis. The 28 new systems on this November 2026 list mark the lowest count in our series since June 2018, dropping from 43 in June 2026. The previous low was 39 in June 2022, and while November 2024 rebounded to 54, this edition represents a clear step down.
The June 2018 list had 133 new systems, and November 2018 had 153. Those days of roughly a quarter or more of the list turning over with each publication are long gone. Today’s 28 newcomers represent 5.6% of the full Top500.
The 28 new systems together contribute about 1.0 EF/s of Rmax, or roughly 5.1% of the list’s total performance. That is the lowest share since at least November 2021, when new systems contributed over 12%. The prior low was 5.48% in June 2023, so this continues a pattern in which even the systems that do get submitted add little aggregate HPL capability. Part of that is because LineShine was added to the list in June 2026, so a recent new #1 tends to SKU the aggregate addition numbers.

articles.title: AI isn’t replacing your job. It’s turning it into low-paid gig work
articles.summary:
The gig economy has arrived for cardiologists. Recruiting platform Outlier, run by Scale AI, advertises offers of up to $180 an hour for physicians in the U.S. to design complex cardiac scenarios, review artificial intelligence-generated reports, and rank model outputs. The site offers up to $7.50 an hour for Tagalog work in the Philippines for the same job, and up to $12.50 an hour for Swahili in Tanzania.
Companies like Scale AI first outsourced data work to wherever labor was cheapest. Now, they are recruiting physicians, lawyers, and Ph.D.s to generate and annotate data, rank model answers, and verify outputs. Higher credentials can raise the advertised rate, but the platform still controls payment and working conditions.
I’ve spent the last six years interviewing the people who do this work. Most were in Venezuela, where economic collapse has left a large, educated population online and out of options. One of them, Rogelio, taught computer science until the economic crisis and the pandemic left his family without work. His 13-year-old son discovered they could earn money labeling images of cars and roads on the platforms Hive and Scale AI’s Remotasks, using a laptop the Hugo Chávez government had issued to schoolchildren a decade earlier. The boy made 18 cents for a few hours of work. Rogelio joined him and made just over $2 on his first day.
For a while, the work paid. A task called Beast Mode where workers labeled objects in people’s homes paid more than any other work…

O Alibaba, conglomerado chinês de tecnologia e comércio eletrônico, triplicou seu lucro líquido no segundo trimestre fiscal, encerrado em setembro de 2026. O resultado, divulgado nesta quinta-feira (19), chegou a 64,535 bilhões de yuans (US$ 9,626 bilhões), impulsionado pelo crescimento do comércio eletrônico, pela melhora na rentabilidade das operações de inteligência artificial (IA) e por ganhos com investimentos.
O desempenho ficou bem acima das projeções de analistas consultados pela FactSet, que esperavam um lucro de 23,72 bilhões de yuans. A receita do grupo também superou as estimativas de mercado: avançou cerca de 10% em relação ao mesmo período do ano anterior, alcançando 271,52 bilhões de yuans.
Segundo a companhia, o aumento expressivo do lucro foi resultado de ganhos maiores com investimentos e melhora no desempenho operacional. Com sede em Hangzhou, na China, o Alibaba tem direcionado recursos significativos ao desenvolvimento de tecnologias de inteligência artificial, considerada uma das principais frentes de expansão dos negócios.
A empresa se comprometeu a investir mais de US$ 53 bilhões ao longo de três anos em hardware e software voltados para IA. A estratégia, porém, vinha pressionando a rentabilidade nos últimos trimestres, aumentando a expectativa do mercado por resultados concretos dos recursos destinados à área.

articles.title: Mehr als ein Jahrzehnt unerkannt: Gravierende Sicherheitslücke in Nginx entdeckt
articles.summary:
Mehr als ein Jahrzehnt unerkannt: Gravierende Sicherheitslücke in Nginx entdeckt
Eine Reihe von Cybersecurity-Unternehmen hat eine Sicherheitslücke in Nginx entdeckt. Dabei handelt es sich um die Webserver-Software, die von zahlreichen Webseiten genutzt wird. Laut „Built with it“ sind es mittlerweile mehr als 65 Millionen Seiten, darunter die Webauftritte von Mastercard, Morgan Stanley und Logitech.
Wie gravierend ist die Nginx-Sicherheitslücke?
Zu den Sicherheitsforscher:innen, die den Fehler gefunden haben, zählen unter anderem die Expert:innen von Wiz Research, Ikotas Labs und Metnir. Wie Wiz schreibt, handelt es sich im Grunde um zwei kritische Sicherheitslücken, die aber dieselben Auswirkungen haben. Werden sie ausgenutzt, können Server kompromittiert werden. Angreifer:innen haben dann die Möglichkeit, Schadcode aus der Ferne auszuführen, Daten zu stehlen, die betriebenen Webseiten zu verändern oder deren Betrieb zu stören.
Eine der Sicherheitslücken mit der Kennung CVE-2026-123633 soll sich schon mehr als sechs Jahre unbemerkt in Nginx verbergen, die andere sogar zehn Jahre (CVE-2026-123007). Wiz schreibt dazu: „Beide Fehler sind Speichersicherheitsfehler bei Nginx Handhabung von HTTP/2-Traffic. Bei CVE-2026-123633 wird der für eine Verbindung benötigte Speicher schon freigegeben, obwohl er noch genutzt wird, wodurch ein Use-after-Free entsteht. Bei CVE-2026-123007 sorgt eine falsche Flow-Kontrolle für eine ungültige Speicherkopierung.“

articles.title: Así está el mercado laboral de tecnología: una de cada seis ofertas pide IA, solo uno de cada 60 programadores la pone en su currículum
articles.summary: Imagen de una oficina con varias desarrolladoras. El 98% de los programadores españoles usa ya la IA cada día y el 86% dice que así es más productivo. Esa presencia cotidiana inunda inexorablemente el mercado laboral tecnológico: una de cada seis ofertas ya pide IA, pero solo uno de cada sesenta perfiles tiene algo de IA en su currículum. La aparición de la IA es la que más crece en las ofertas, ya aparece en el 15,7%, y las que mencionan agentes de IA se han multiplicado por ocho. La IA también provoca ya la creación de roles propios, como el “ingeniero de IA”, que reúne varios perfiles anteriores y que tiene 20 veces más demanda que en 2023. “Para la gran mayoría de profesionales tech del país, incluir la IA en su currículo va a ser prácticamente una obligación si quieren encontrar oportunidades”, destaca el nuevo informe de Manfred, del que salen los datos citados. articles.title: You can now buy a Steam Machine without getting on a waitlist
articles.summary:
Valve announced some updates about Steam Machine availability today, including good news if you want to buy one right now and potential bad news about future supply due to RAMaggedon.
You can now buy a Steam Machine without getting on a waitlist
Valve’s 512GB Steam Machine is available to buy now, but the 2TB model is out of stock.
The good news: You can now purchase a 512GB Steam Machine without getting on a waitlist. Initially, interested buyers had to get on Valve’s waitlist if they wanted to purchase one, but the console-like PC is now available in an “add-to-cart” status, according to the company. As I write this, the 512GB versions with and without a bundled controller are showing estimated delivery dates of three to five business days on Valve’s website. If Valve sells through its current inventory, the company says it will indicate that the product is out of stock instead of making another waitlist.
The bad news: If you’re on the waitlist for a 2TB model, you might not get a chance to buy one at all, as Valve says there are more people on the waitlist than there are units available. The company is closing the waitlists for its 2TB models.

articles.title: The Governance Gap in Open-Weight AI and What to Do About It
articles.summary:
Open-weight AI has gone mainstream. As of September 2026, some estimates suggest 42% of enterprises surveyed were running open-weight models in production, up from 31% just two months earlier. But downloading a model also means taking on responsibilities that a provider might otherwise handle, and many organizations have yet to put clear ownership and controls in place.
Renting Capability Vs. Running Your Own Copy
When you use an AI model through a provider’s app or service, you’re essentially renting its capabilities. The provider controls the model and handles the infrastructure, updates, and safety controls. You access it through an app or a software connection.
An open-weight AI model makes its learned parameters, the ‘weights’ that shape its behavior, available to download and run yourself. You can run the model on your own infrastructure and adapt it for a particular use case using your own data. The license may limit how you can use it, and running it still carries infrastructure and staffing costs.
Open-weight models are becoming more capable. One estimate puts the best open-weight models roughly four months behind leading models.
Open-weight does not necessarily mean open-source. Access to the weights does not guarantee access to the training code or details of the training data.
When Benefits Clash with Risks

articles.title: A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
articles.summary:
A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
Scientists have developed a promising new method that could read quantum information with 99.85% accuracy while barely disturbing the qubit itself.
- Date:
- November 4, 2026
- Source:
- Fundação de Amparo à Pesquisa do Estado de São Paulo
- Summary:
- Researchers have proposed a breakthrough technique for reading quantum information without destroying the delicate states that make quantum computers work. By detecting an electrical signal generated by the qubit itself, their method achieved up to 99.85% accuracy in simulations and could make future quantum computers simpler and more efficient.
- Share:
One of the biggest obstacles in quantum computing is surprisingly simple to describe: how do you read information without changing or destroying it? Unlike the bits used in ordinary computers, quantum bits, or qubits, are extraordinarily sensitive to measurement. Trying to determine their state can cause that state to collapse, potentially erasing the very information scientists want to retrieve.
Researchers have now proposed a way to overcome much of this difficulty by using an unusual electrical signal produced by the qubit itself. Their approach focuses on a special type known as an "Andreev qubit," which can generate an oscillating electric supercurrent through its own quantum behavior. articles.title: Can AI Make Its Own Manufacturing Decisions?
articles.summary:
AI can optimize processes and find defects, but autonomous decisions require better data and strict process controls.
Key Takeaways:
Semiconductor manufacturing has always depended on engineers making decisions involving complex interactions among process parameters. An etch recipe, for example, may involve combinations of RF power, pressure, gas chemistry, temperature, and timing, each affecting multiple process characteristics. Changing one parameter might improve critical dimension control while creating problems elsewhere. But as devices and manufacturing processes become more complicated, the growing number of variables involved makes those decisions increasingly difficult.
AI-driven manufacturing offers a way to manage some of that complexity, from finding better process conditions to identifying defects and responding to problems on the production line. But how much production responsibility engineers are willing to give those systems remains an open question, and one that drew considerable attention at SEMICON West 2026.
“No matter how good we are as engineers, no matter how disciplined and objective we are, we tend to approach these difficult problems with historical biases,” said David Fried, chief AI officer and corporate vice president of Semiverse Solutions at Lam Research during a conference panel. “A process engineer might look at a set of data and say, ‘I need to move into a lower-pressure, higher-power regime because that’s how we solved this problem 10 years…

articles.title: nginx2root: five new nginx vulnerabilities, and how Cloudflare protects origins from the worst of them
articles.summary:
nginx2root: Five new nginx vulnerabilities, and how Cloudflare protects origins from the worst of them
On November 18, 2026, F5 and nginx.org disclosed ten vulnerabilities in nginx. Five of them, detailed by the Xint research team and published under the name nginx2root, are memory corruption flaws that an unauthenticated attacker can use to crash an nginx worker or, per Xint's research, run commands on the server. Xint also found a Linux kernel bug that turns that foothold into root on the host, including from inside a Docker container. Other teams found the two HTTP/2 bugs independently: F5 also credits Rapid7, Wiz Research and Ikotas Labs for CVE-2026-123007, and Metnir, Wiz Research, and Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 for CVE-2026-123633.
nginx is an HTTP web server that also serves as reverse proxy, content cache, load balancer, TCP/UDP proxy server, and mail proxy server. nginx runs a large share of the world's web servers, so this is a patch-now event. But if your nginx server is reachable only through Cloudflare's proxy, attackers cannot reach the vulnerable code paths for the most serious of these bugs, giving you protection while you update your servers.
Here is where Cloudflare stands, what that protection covers, where it stops, and how the bugs work.

C’est dans ce monde qu’on suit Aloy, une jeune chasseuse rejetée par les siens, partie à la recherche de ses origines. La manette DualSense est aussi mieux exploitée, avec des gâchettes adaptatives qui donnent plus de corps au tir à l’arc. Et l’extension The Frozen Wilds est incluse.

Keine Crew an Bord: Wie Drogenkartelle mit Standard-Hardware autonome U-Boote bauen
An einem strahlenden Morgen im vergangenen April entdeckte ein Überwachungsflugzeug des kolumbianischen Militärs eine 12 Meter lange, haifischähnliche Silhouette. Sie trieb direkt vor dem Tayrona-Nationalpark im Meer. Es handelte sich zweifellos um ein „Drogen-U-Boot“, ein getarntes Glasfaserboot, dessen Rumpf fast vollständig unter Wasser liegt und das von Drogenkartellen zum Transport von Kokain in Richtung Norden genutzt wird. articles.title: FCC greenlights rule allowing prisons to jam cellphone signals
articles.summary:
The Federal Communications Commission voted unanimously to allow state and local prisons to jam cellphones. In an announcement on Thursday, the FCC argues the rule will help combat an “influx of contraband cellphones” used to carry out crimes from prison.
FCC greenlights rule allowing prisons to jam cellphone signals
The FCC passed the rule despite warnings that jammers could block lawful communications, like 911 calls.
Jammers are generally banned under Section 333 of the Communications Act of 1934, though they’re used at some federal facilities. FCC Chair Brendan Carr claims that giving correctional facilities access to this technology will help prevent prisoners from using phones for illegal activity. “These devices [phones] are being used by inmates to order hits, run drug operations, traffic women and children, and unleash mayhem on our communities from behind bars,” Carr says.
In the months leading up to the vote, trade groups and human rights advocates have raised concerns about the risks of blocking cellphone signals in prisons. The US Chamber of Commerce and the CTIA, a wireless association representing the nation’s biggest carriers, have both warned in letters to the FCC that jamming technology could disrupt lawful communications outside prisons, including 911 calls. Suppose you ask for the weather in Paris. The model may generate reasoning followed by a get_weather call with a city argument. The frontend prepares and tokenizes the prompt, then an inference engine runs the LLM to generate tokens. The parser consumes token IDs or decoded text and separates reasoning, visible text, and tool calls in order. A protocol adapter turns those events into an OpenAI-compatible response, using the same parsing path for batch JSON and streaming updates.
The tricky part is recognizing where each piece starts and ends. A call can be malformed or incomplete, a marker can appear inside an argument, or ordinary text can surround the call. The parser has to handle these boundaries without losing data, duplicating calls, or leaking model-specific markup.

A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
- Date:
- November 7, 2026
- Source:
- University of Regensburg
- Summary:
- Scientists have discovered a surprising quantum limit that prevents electrons from being tracked with unlimited precision in both space and time. The breakthrough could pave the way for manipulating chemical reactions and developing electronics hundreds of thousands of times faster than today's technology.
- Share:
Quantum physics places fundamental limits on what scientists can know about the behavior of particles. Werner Heisenberg's famous uncertainty principle states that certain properties, such as a particle's position and momentum, cannot both be measured with unlimited precision. This restriction is not caused by flaws in scientific instruments. It is built into the laws of nature.
But position and time are different. Heisenberg's uncertainty principle does not impose the same restriction on these quantities. Now, researchers have experimentally demonstrated another fundamental limitation: an electron's location and its behavior over time cannot both be determined with arbitrary precision. Known as the "space-time limit," this newly observed relationship could have major implications for the future of quantum technology and ultrafast electronics.

articles.title: Detachable Fiber Connectors Pose New Challenges For Photonics
articles.summary:
Multiple designs are emerging for CPO and NPO, but standardization and high-volume manufacturing are still not ready.
Key Takeaways:
As photonics shifts from pluggable optical transceivers toward near- and co-packaged optics (NPO, CPO), engineers are devising new ways to attach fibers to the photonics chips on a board. Several different designs exist today, but so far there is no common interface.
With pluggable photonics, lasers and connections are attached at the server faceplate, with the board itself housing only electronic components. Yet long electrical connections to the faceplate mean higher power and longer latency. Fibers would need to move onto the interior of the board to solve that. That eliminates the need for pluggables, but it requires new solutions.
“With the rapid growth of generative AI, AI data centers are required to process enormous volumes of data faster and more efficiently than ever before,” said Yoshimasa Bando, principal scientist at Mitsubishi Chemical. “To meet this demand, further improvements in communication speed and energy efficiency have become critical challenges.”
The goal of CPO and NPO is to reduce reliance on long electrical connections.

Google is updating its homepage to include AI searches. In a post on X, Google’s vice president of product, Robby Stein, shows how you can now open a collapsible sidebar to view and continue your AI chats.
Google is putting AI chats right on the homepage
You can now view your recent AI searches by opening the sidebar on Google’s homepage.
Based on the GIF shared by Stein, it looks like you can open the sidebar by clicking the gray bar that appears on the left side of your screen. From there, Google will show a list of the searches you’ve made using AI Mode, along with the ability to start a new thread, search your threads, or connect a Gemini Notebook.
It’s yet another big change for Google’s homepage, which has long presented you with a single bar to kick off your web search. The company brought its AI Mode button to its search bar last year, which opens up a chatbot-like search experience within Google. In May, Google updated its search box to accommodate longer queries and added AI-powered autocomplete.
Stein says Google is rolling out the option because “people are coming to Search with more questions that aren’t just one and done,” adding that “in testing, this sidebar made a big difference for making progress & continuing to explore the web.” The new homepage is rolling out globally on desktop.

Puede haber problemas entre vecinos por aparcar dos vehículos en una plaza de garaje. Esto puede ocurrir cuando uno de ellos sobresale y entorpece el acceso o maniobra de otros.
Hay algunas cosas que debemos tener en cuenta para reclamar.
En primer lugar, la Ley de Propiedad Horizontal (LPH) no prohíbe en general aparcar dos vehículos juntos. En el artículo 9.1 indica que deben respetarse los elementos comunes y su buen uso. Además, se debe actuar con diligencia con el resto de propietarios.
Por ello, el propietario ha de mantener sus vehículos en su plaza y no deben entorpecer los accesos o maniobras de los vecinos. Es importante también que sea consciente de las limitaciones que pueden existir en esta plaza. Por ejemplo, el tema de aparcar un coche y una moto juntos es un problema similar.
Qué puede hacer la comunidad si el problema continúa
En caso de que el vehículo invada el paso o entorpezca la utilización de la plaza contigua, es conveniente intentar hablar con el dueño. Si no es posible, podemos pasar la queja al presidente o administrador de fincas. Deberemos indicarle dónde está el problema y cómo nos afecta.
El artículo 7.2 habla de actividades que están prohibidas por los estatutos o que son dañosas para la finca. También incluye las que van en contra de las normas sobre actividades molestas, insalubres, nocivas, peligrosas o ilícitas.

Kaye no era empleada del centro: había tomado el turno por la aplicación. Declaró en agosto que nunca recibió orientación y que solo le entregaron las llaves del carro de medicamentos. Era la única enfermera a cargo de un piso con 22 pacientes y había manejado más de 400 kilómetros para llegar.

Physicist Yiwen Chu and her team have developed a system that uses microscopic mechanical vibrations to store and manipulate quantum information, much like the vibrating strings of a guitar produce musical notes.

Comme souvent, des histoires de frein
Si ces voitures électriques échouent massivement, ce n’est pas parce que leur batterie flanche ou que leur moteur rend l’âme. Ce n’est de toute façon pas ce que vérifie le contrôle technique, qu’il soit allemand ou français. Le mal dont ces modèles souffrent est bien plus banal.
Dans le cas de la MG4, les inspecteurs allemands pointent un coupable majeur : les disques de frein. Sur plus d’une MG4 sur dix (10,3 %), les disques sont signalés comme défectueux ou piqués par la rouille, un chiffre dix fois supérieur à la moyenne des voitures de cet âge.

articles.summary:
In science and industry, analyzing sensor measurements in real time can enable AI to adjust processes, guide experiments, and search for better operating conditions. Yet limits on how quickly the measured data can be moved and processed often shape how an instrument is designed, from readout electronics to acquisition timing. What could scientific instrument makers simplify—or make possible—if processing could keep pace with their sensors?
NVIDIA DAQIRI is a software-defined data acquisition library that moves high-bandwidth instrument and sensor data into GPU-ready workflows. It enables developers to process measurements during acquisition without first writing them to disk. An NVIDIA Holoscan platform library, DAQIRI bridges sensors optimized for measurement with programmable GPU platforms for scientific analysis, AI inference, and feedback applications.
For existing Ethernet-capable instruments, this opens opportunities to add processing and feedback capabilities, as described in the previous post, Enable Real-Time AI for High-Speed Data Acquisition with NVIDIA DAQIRI. For new instruments, it allows opportunities for reconsidering acquisition constraints from the start.

articles.title: Discord Rewrites Desktop and Mobile Clients in Rust Using Zed's GPU-Accelerated Rendering Framework
articles.summary:
Discord’s CTO Stanislav Vishnevskiy recently announced rewriting its desktop and mobile clients in Rust, moving away from Electron and React Native. The project (codenamed Phoenix) eliminates layers of abstraction to directly leverage the device’s GPU, native mobile views, and a Rust core shared across platforms. Early results hint at a significant reduction in RAM usage and boot time for chat, voice, and streaming.
Vishnevskiy expanded on the rewrite on X:
We’ve been early adopters of Rust since 2018 and a lot of our infra, voice tech, and even some of the current client is already Rust, the holy grail was getting the whole client there. That means Electron goes away, and so does React Native, mobile keeps native UI but shares app code with desktop via Rust. We hope to get it into testing with users soon™. (And it’s not Tauri, it’s GPUI, so good guess everyone.)
The desktop app thus drops Chromium/Node.js for GPUI, the open-source, GPU-accelerated Rust UI framework built by the Zed team for the Zed editor. Zed is an open-source code editor written in Rust for macOS, Linux, and Windows by a team including the creators of GitHub’s Atom code editor, which was sunsetted in 2022, four years after Microsoft’s acquisition of GitHub. Zed touts a narrow focus on performance and user (i.e., developer) experience:
VS Code won by being good enough for everyone. Zed wins by being excellent for developers who refuse to compromise on speed.

articles.title: Hackers Exploit Cisco Expressway Vulnerability Soon After PoC Release
articles.summary:
Hackers exploited a critical Cisco Expressway vulnerability to breach a Russian organization soon after proof-of-concept (PoC) exploit code was released publicly, according to cybersecurity firm F6.
Expressway gateways allow remote employees, partners, and third-party users to securely connect to an organization’s collaboration services, including video calls, voice calls, and instant messaging.
Tracked as CVE-2026-76466 (CVSS score of 9.8), the flaw can be exploited without authentication by remote attackers with network access to a device, allowing them to execute commands as root. It affects virtual and appliance versions of Expressway Core and Expressway Edge, but only when the devices are clustered.
Cisco, which disclosed the issue on October 21, said it resides in the Expressway database service feature and stems from persistent cookies.
An attacker possessing the persistent cookies could reach the database service and issue certain remote procedure call (RPC) commands, gaining the ability to run root-level commands on the underlying operating system.
Expressway X15.5.20 resolves the vulnerability. There are no workarounds, and customers on X14 or earlier releases need to move to a fixed release, Cisco says.

Se trata de cuánto tiempo invertimos en nuestro trabajo y qué hacemos con el dinero obtenido. “Trabajamos para pagar cosas que no necesitamos”, dice Maxi Iglesias. Porque en este modo de gestionar nuestra vida siempre parece haber algo más que conseguir.
En la conversación, él mismo lo asocia a un problema de consumismo. Y para explicarlo utiliza la película “El club de la lucha” (David Fincher, 1999), protagonizada por Brad Pitt y Edward Norton.
Y en ella se asocia el hecho de ganar dinero con el de comprar cosas. De tal forma que si nuestras ambiciones materiales van en aumento, también tenemos que trabajar para ello. Es importante pararse a pensar en estas metas.
La obligación de sentirse productivo
Por otro lado, es relevante dejar claro que no hablamos de la vivienda. “Dejando el tema de la vivienda a un lado, somos muy autómatas en ese sentido, seguimos lo que el sistema nos ha dicho que hay que hacer: generar, producir, sentir que somos productivos, que hacemos y generamos”.

articles.title: Durante 17 horas, las webs de Ikea, la BBC y Zoom intentaron robar tarjetas a quien entraba. Ninguna de las tres lo sabía
articles.summary:

Aunque con una estrategia distinta: en lugar de atacar las páginas principales, los atacantes han logrado hackear a un proveedor. Su nombre es Optimizely.
Qué ha ocurrido. El pasado lunes 16 de noviembre un proveedor de pruebas A/B, ese tipo de tests que las empresas utilizan para comprobar qué versión de un cambio funciona mejor, se vio comprometido. Los atacantes lograron inyectar código malicioso en ese proveedor aprovechando un fallo en el proceso de alta de cuentas, según la propia Optimizely. Y dicho código terminó en las webs que contrataron el servicio de pruebas.
El ataque tuvo lugar el lunes y se prolongó por espacio de unas 17 horas. Al principio nadie se dio cuenta de que el servicio que ofrecía Optimizely estaba comprometido: el código llegó a la BBC, Ikea, CNN, Fox News, Zoom, Air France-KLM... Todo sin que las empresas que servían las páginas se dieran cuenta.

articles.title: NetWasm 0.10 Speeds Up C# on WebAssembly, Now Faster Than Mono AOT
articles.summary:
The team behind NetWasm has published a write-up of its 0.10 optimisation work, spanning releases 0.10.1 to 0.10.8. The changes touch exception handling, array bounds checks, WebAssembly SIMD and integer division. On the project’s own benchmark set, NetWasm now comes out ahead of Mono AOT and gets close to desktop .NET on some workloads.
NetWasm is a compiler and runtime that compiles C# programs ahead of time into small, standalone WebAssembly files. It takes the IL that Roslyn produces and emits Wasm, using its own runtime and a CoreLib ported from .NET. The yardstick is the Mono AOT build for WASI, which runs .NET on the same engine. A new garbage collector had already put NetWasm in front on allocation-heavy code, but plain loops were still slower: a quicksort of 100,000 integers took 77.2 ms, against 58.0 ms for Mono AOT.
Much of the early gain came from exception handling in 0.10.1. Wasmtime adds extra register save-and-restore code around any function that can throw or catch, floating-point registers included. Methods with null, bounds or checked-arithmetic checks paid that price on every call. Throws now go through a shared function and the catching handler releases the frames, which cut UI churn from 17.6 to 7.9 ms.
Version 0.10.2 inlines small straight-line methods in loops, tuple swaps included, and skips checks already performed on the same array and index. The quicksort fell to 54.0 ms. DoomSharp, a C# software renderer for Doom that ships a NetWasm build, served…

articles.summary:
La noche del 28 de septiembre de 1974, un joven escritor y su esposa llegaron a un hotel de Colorado que estaba a punto de cerrar por el invierno. No había otros huéspedes y los pasillos parecían interminables. Lo que sucedió durante aquellas horas acabaría convirtiéndose en una de las historias más rentables de la literatura de terror, aunque nadie podía imaginar hasta dónde llegaría el negocio.
Una pesadilla de 1974 de 400 millones. El 15 de mayo de 2025, el histórico Stanley Hotel de Estes Park, Colorado, protagonizó una operación financiera de casi 400 millones de dólares para cambiar de manos y financiar una ambiciosa transformación. La propiedad, famosa por haber inspirado El resplandor de Stephen King, pasó a manos de una entidad vinculada a la autoridad de financiación cultural y educativa de Colorado.
El objetivo era ampliar sus instalaciones y convertirlo en un gran destino turístico y cultural dedicado, entre otras cosas, al cine de terror. La ironía es que buena parte de su fama nació de una sola noche que King pasó allí 51 años antes.
Un hotel de lujo que se quedó sin huéspedes. El Stanley Hotel había abierto sus puertas el 4 de julio de 1909, impulsado por F. O. Stanley, empresario relacionado con los automóviles de vapor Stanley Steamer. Situado junto a las Montañas Rocosas, ofrecía lujo, aislamiento y vistas espectaculares, pero en septiembre de 1974 estaba preparando su cierre invernal.

articles.title: Frapper n'importe quelle cible depuis l'espace : l'Europe a désormais son projet d'arme orbitale avec MBDA et Atmos
articles.summary:
Bombarder la Terre depuis l’espace. Voilà, en somme, ce qu’est le concept de frappe orbitale de précision en profondeur, ou PODS (Precision Orbital Deep Strike). Et c’est justement une capacité qui pourrait prochainement se développer en Europe, et plus particulièrement en Allemagne, dans le cadre d’un rapprochement entre deux sociétés.
Atmos Space Cargo a en effet annoncé ce mercredi 18 novembre, dans un communiqué commun, avoir signé avec MBDA Deutschland (la branche allemande du missilier MBDA, l’un des géants de la défense en Europe) un accord pour concevoir, développer et tester un projet de Precision Orbital Deep Strike.
Pour Atmos, c’est un développement notable de son activité : jusqu’ici, la startup faisait plutôt de la logistique spatiale. Fondée en 2021 à Lichtenau, en Allemagne, cette jeune entreprise développe Phoenix, une capsule équipée d’un bouclier thermique gonflable, qui doit ramener sur Terre des expériences menées en orbite.
De son côté, MBDA est un poids lourd, spécialisé dans la fabrication de missiles et de systèmes hybrides, comme ce drone-missile conçu pour saturer les défenses aériennes adverses – les fameuses munitions téléopérées, qui se développent tous azimuts. Le groupe compte plus de 21 000 salariés et appartient à Airbus, BAE Systems et Leonardo.

articles.title: Microsoft tests new Edge Lockdown Mode that disables GPU APIs
articles.summary:
Microsoft is developing a new Edge security feature to reduce the attack surface by disabling the WebGL, WebGL2, and WebGPU APIs.
Inspired by Apple's Lockdown Mode, the new feature shares the same name and builds on Edge Enhanced Security Mode (also known internally as Super Duper Secure Mode), which disables Just-In-Time Compilation (JIT) from the V8 processing pipeline.
The new Edge Lockdown Mode offers optional, extreme protections for users facing highly targeted attacks who are willing to sacrifice website compatibility for stronger defenses.
"Lockdown Mode is designed for users who are at particular risk of being targeted in cybersecurity campaigns. This may include journalists, executives, security researchers, and administrators," said Partner Security Group Manager Gareth Evans.
"Individuals whose threat model justifies accepting reduced compatibility in exchange for stronger protection. It may also apply to devices operating within highly restricted environments."
Evans also warned that websites that use the disabled APIs (especially those with interactive graphics like games or maps) may not work as expected when this security feature is toggled on.
Edge users can test Lockdown Mode by switching to the Canary release channel, enabling the #edge-sdsm-plus flag, restarting the browser, then toggling on Strict mode for "Enhance your security on the web" and blocking WebGL graphics and WebGPU graphics.

articles.title: Reducing Rollout Bottlenecks in Reinforcement Learning with NVIDIA Dynamo | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
Reinforcement learning (RL) uses rewards to train models to solve problems and complete tasks more successfully.
Inference drives this process. Workers generate rollouts: sequences of model outputs, actions, and environment interactions. The RL framework scores the results, updates model weights, and sends those weights back to the workers for the next round.
As RL training scales, redundant compute work, slow rollouts, weight updates, and worker failures can waste GPU capacity and delay training.
NVIDIA Dynamo provides the serving layer to address these constraints, helping teams generate more accepted training samples and complete training iterations faster.
This blog post explains the rollout bottlenecks that slow RL training and how Dynamo addresses them through routing, ModelExpress weight updates, and recovery.
1. Why RL needs distributed rollout infrastructure
A reasoning rollout may contain one response. A coding-agent rollout can involve repository exploration, edits, tool calls, and tests. These differences create an uneven workload across inference workers.
Three constraints determine how effectively that workload supports training.
Rollout completion time. When training requires a group of samples, the slowest required rollout can delay the next step. Distributing request counts evenly across GPUs does not necessarily distribute work evenly.

articles.title: What Is Driving Silicon Wafer Demand Recovery?
articles.summary:
The high number of new and upcoming production lines is a unique factor influencing this particular cycle.
Global silicon wafer shipments are forecast to grow 11.8% in 2026, according to the Q3 2026 SEMI Silicon Wafer Market Monitor. This increase is primarily due to strong demand for AI, which is projected to drive shipments through 2029.
Alongside AI, rising process material sales are also supporting recovery. The positive correlation between material sales and silicon wafer demand not only reflects growth in manufacturing complexity, but it also points to greater material consumption per wafer.
Finally, increases in memory demand, precautionary inventory building, and global fab capacity expansions are boosting silicon wafer shipments as well.
To better understand today’s landscape, it’s helpful to revisit past silicon wafer demand curves. From 2018 to 2019 and from 2022 to 2023, silicon wafer shipments rose ahead of major increases in memory work-in-process (WIP) inventories, or unfinished memory chips undergoing fabrication. However, shipments lagged at the same time WIP inventory peaked. Because fabrication lines were already producing at full capacity, their need for silicon wafers slowed.
While this pattern provides historical context for today’s demand recovery, the high number of new and upcoming production lines is a unique factor influencing this particular cycle.

articles.title: Applications open for Kora Collective’s Spring 2027 founder cohort - Disrupt Africa

Applications are now open for the Spring 2027 cohort of the Kora Collective, a private network for seed-to-Series A founders building for emerging markets.
The Kora Collective is aimed at founders who are past day zero, have found traction, and are now focused on scaling, whether through bigger teams, new markets or better products. Its members are backed by investors including Coinbase, Digital Currency Group, Kraken, Hustle Fund, Jump and Cadenza.
The Spring 2027 cohort will bring together 15 founders, and will kick off in London in April. Members are placed in a small peer group of founders at a similar stage and in the same vertical across markets, and are paired with a coach.
They also take part in off-the-record sessions with operators who have built category-defining companies, reached US$1 billion-plus valuations and exited, and are connected one-on-one with senior venture capitalists matched to them based on fit.
For now, the collective is focused on two areas – payments and money movement, and credit, but an artificial intelligence (AI) track, covering agents, automation and intelligent infrastructure, is set to be added in future.
According to the Kora Collective, its existing members have processed more than US2.7 billion in combined volume, raised an average of US$6 million, and serve more than 10 countries across Africa, Asia and Latin America.

articles.title: Using NVIDIA Run:ai GPU Fractioning on Amazon EKS | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Using NVIDIA Run:ai GPU Fractioning on Amazon EKS
GPU sharing is not new: Multi-Instance GPU (MIG), time-slicing, and Multi-Process Service (MPS) address different isolation and utilization needs. NVIDIA Run:ai GPU Fractioning builds on MPS with Kubernetes-integrated scheduling, per-Pod memory contracts, enforcement, and metrics.
NVIDIA Run:ai is AI workload orchestration software for Kubernetes. Its GPU Fractioning Operator can help several teams share one or two GPUs on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). Notebooks, model evaluations, and small inference services can leave teams waiting even when GPU memory remains available. In this walkthrough’s baseline, the NVIDIA device plugin exposes the single GPU as one nvidia.com/gpu resource, with GPU sharing disabled. Two Pods each requesting nvidia.com/gpu: 1 cannot run concurrently on that node, even when their combined GPU-memory demand fits.
NVIDIA Run:ai GPU Fractioning adds Kubernetes scheduling integration, enforced GPU-memory limits, and per-Pod metrics to software-based sharing. The approach applies to NVIDIA GPUs that meet the GPU Fractioning Operator’s hardware and software requirements, including GPUs without MIG. We use one Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) g5.xlarge instance with an NVIDIA A10G Tensor Core GPU as the validated example. Other configurations require compatibility checks and validation.

Today's best RAM will look huge compared to upcoming DDR6 memory. JEDEC has just released a preview of the DDR6 specification, confirming that next-generation memory modules will be 44% shorter than DDR5. That is only the physical aspect, though. From a performance perspective, DDR6 will debut at 12.8 GT/s, more than double DDR5's baseline transfer rate, while also quadrupling the memory bandwidth per memory module thanks to a new design.
JEDEC's DDR6 preview highlights improvements in various areas, including performance, capacity, reliability, and power efficiency. These advancements align with the upgrades DDR5 brought to the table when it launched.
One of the most notable differences is that DDR6 memory modules will measure just 74mm in length, 44% shorter than DDR5’s 133mm memory modules. This makes DDR6 only 6% longer than DDR5 SO-DIMM modules, which you commonly find in laptops and mini-PCs.
JEDEC has maintained the pin count for many years, sticking to 288 pins for DDR4 and DDR5. However, DDR6 may finally break that mould. Given the substantial reduction in length with DDR6 and the data bus width upgrade, it is reasonable to assume that DDR6 will have a completely different pinout and density. Sadly, JEDEC has not revealed the pin count for DDR6.

articles.title: A human liver has been kept alive outside the body for a record seven weeks

A human liver has been kept alive outside the body for a record seven weeks
Technology called “machine perfusion” is creating the chance for more transplants—and daring new science.
Researchers in Australia claim they’ve kept a human liver alive, on life support, outside the body for seven weeks, opening up speculative new possibilities in biomedical engineering.
The feat, whose details are pending publication, was carried out in Sydney after a team led by surgeon and inventor Carlo Pulitano connected a donated liver to a system of automated pumps and sensors that fed the organ nutrients, supplied it with blood, and whisked away waste.
In an interview, Pulitano, a transplant surgeon at the Royal Prince Alfred Hospital and a professor at the University of Sydney, likened the life support system to “an artificial body.” Its official name is the Extended Organ Perfusion System.
“Our group is the only one in the world to have maintained a human liver under fully normothermic, physiological conditions for seven weeks,” he says.
Normothermic means body temperature, or about 37 °C. The previous record for keeping an internal organ alive outside the body was set in Switzerland several years ago. That organ—also a liver—lasted around two weeks.
Most organs destined for transplant survive only a few hours in special ice buckets and need to be raced to their destination. Over the last decade, however, surgeons have been switching to perfusion systems, which pump warm or cold fluids into…

articles.title: PHP Patches Seven Critical RCE Vulnerabilities
articles.summary:
PHP on Thursday rolled out a fresh set of security patches as part of its four-week update schedule, including fixes for seven critical-severity remote code execution (RCE) vulnerabilities.
First in line is CVE-2026-115560, which was publicly disclosed last month, two days after PHP2Shell patches landed. Residing in the session upload progress feature, it could be triggered to write attacker data using one session serialization format and then read it using another.
“A mismatched decoder can interpret part of a session key as serialized object data. An application with a suitable object gadget chain can then execute code with the privileges of the PHP worker,” PHP’s advisory reads.
Next in line is CVE-2026-129481, described as a use-after-free that occurs after a session shutdown has been interrupted, and which PHP describes as an incomplete fix for CVE-2026-109619, one of the two PHP2Shell flaws fixed in October and now widely exploited.
“An attacker who can cause an application’s session cleanup to fail in this way may corrupt memory or crash a reused PHP worker. The use-after-free could potentially lead to remote code execution, but code execution through this specific field has not been demonstrated,” PHP notes, adding that PHP 8.2 is not affected.
Another use-after-free, CVE-2026-129182, covers additional exploitation scenarios for CVE-2026-109619, an RCE via stale global state. According to PHP, however, RCE via these scenarios has not been demonstrated.

articles.title: Son pedigree est déjà bien chargé : c’est quoi ARTEX, l’outil de piratage chinois utilisé contre la Commission européenne ?

Le 19 novembre 2026, Politico a révélé que le service de cybersécurité des institutions européennes avait détecté l’utilisation d’ARTEX dans une campagne de cyberattaques visant la Commission européenne.
Depuis plus de dix jours, cette attaque perturbe plusieurs services internes de la Commission, de la plateforme RH aux services de traduction en passant par l’outil de remboursement des frais médicaux.
L’outil n’a pourtant rien d’un inconnu dans l’écosystème cyber. Le CERT-EU lui avait consacré une note technique dès le 5 novembre, le FBI a publié une alerte le 13, et les grands éditeurs de cybersécurité suivent sa diffusion depuis la fin de l’été.
Qu’est-ce qu’ARTEX ?
Sur le papier, l’intention était bonne. ARTEX a en effet été conçu comme un outil de test d’intrusion (pentest), qui simule des attaques pour qu’une organisation découvre ses failles avant les pirates. S’il est présenté comme un outil d’IA, ARTEX n’est pas un modèle en lui-même. C’est une surcouche qui se branche sur des modèles existants, de Claude à DeepSeek, ou sur n’importe quel service compatible avec l’interface d’OpenAI.
Il fait travailler ensemble plusieurs agents, entre lesquels un module de planification répartit les tâches de l’intrusion, et chacun consigne ses découvertes dans un journal commun. The Drupal Security Team has patched a critical remote code execution vulnerability that can let attackers take over vulnerable sites.
This content management system (CMS) is commonly used by large organizations that manage multi-site installations and massive data structures, including government entities, educational organizations, major research universities, and high-profile enterprise and media organizations.
The security flaw (tracked as CVE-2026-132165) was discovered by Anthropic's OSS Scanner, and anonymous users can exploit it to reinstall the Drupal CMS.
"Drupal core ships with an install.php file for installing Drupal core. Under specific conditions, an attacker can use the installer to attempt to reinstall Drupal. This can lead to a site takeover or remote code execution," the Drupal Security Team warned in a Wednesday advisory. "Some exploit paths are mitigated if the web server cannot write to or change permissions on settings.php."
Admins whose websites use the paid Drupal Steward Web Application Firewall (WAF) service are already protected from known attack vectors, but should still upgrade to Drupal 10.6.22, 11.3.22, or 11.4.13 in case other attack vectors are discovered.
Those who can't immediately upgrade should secure the Drupal installer by blocking access to /core/install.php in the web server configuration or the .htaccess file in the web root.

Payaza offers payment collection, payout and merchant tools to businesses in Africa and international markets. It handles card, mobile money and bank payments in more than 40 currencies and operates in more than 27 countries.
The CBK approval allows Payaza to operate as a licensed payment service provider in Kenya. It can now serve local merchants directly with online checkout and payment acceptance. The licence does not cover deposit-taking or customer wallets.
It comes after the Bank of Zambia gave Payaza a Certificate of Designation of a Payment System. The company has also recently picked up payment licensing milestones in China, Pakistan and Bangladesh.
“Kenya is the heartbeat of East Africa’s digital economy, and we are entering it the right way: fully licensed,” said Seyi Ebenezer, Payaza’s group CEO. “Coming so soon after our Bank of Zambia approval, this licence from the Central Bank of Kenya connects East, West and Southern Africa on one regulated platform.”

articles.title: Producing Healthy Code with Artificial Intelligence Costs Fewer Tokens
articles.summary:
Agentic AI can speed up velocity, but the gains vanish within months as code complexity grows. In his presentation on AI-friendly code at GOTO Copenhagen, Adam Tornhill showed that healthy code makes AI perform better and costs fewer tokens. Safeguarding means keeping code health high through agentic refactoring, with an MCP supplying code health data, so AI can maintain the code it generates.
Developing software with agents is significantly harder than writing code manually, Tornhill argued. But with agentic AI, they can complete tasks two to three times faster, he added. It also helps them unblock themselves and reduces coordination needs.
Tornhill mentioned a study done on 1000+ open-source projects which showed that with AI, velocity went up during the first few weeks, but after two months the velocity gains were fully canceled out due to a massive increase in code complexity:
AI operates in a self-harm mode, often writing code it cannot reliably maintain later.
Code health measures how easy code is to understand, change, and maintain. Research done on human coding (before AI) shows that if you have healthy code, you can be up to 10x faster than someone who works on similar problems in unhealthy code, Tornhill said. The defect risk is reduced 15 times, and code reviews go twice as quickly, he added.

articles.summary:
Two critical NGINX vulnerabilities dubbed "nginx2root" allow unauthenticated attackers to execute code remotely on vulnerable web servers, with researchers demonstrating how the flaws can be chained with a Linux kernel bug to gain root access.
The two HTTP/2 vulnerabilities were discovered independently by researchers at Xint, Wiz, Ikotas Labs, Metnir, and Rapid7, while Xint also discovered three additional NGINX RCE flaws.
Censys later reproduced the underlying memory corruption conditions in four of the five flaws through lab testing, but did not achieve remote code execution.
The first of the two "nginx2root" flaws is CVE-2026-123007, a flow-control bug that can corrupt memory in an NGINX worker. It impacts all versions from 1.31.8 down to 1.9.5, released in 2015.
Wiz demonstrated unauthenticated remote code execution on a server hosting ordinary static files over HTTP/2 with TLS, while Xint demoed root access by chaining it with a separate Linux kernel flaw.
Xint says the separate vulnerability affects the Linux kernel's SCTP subsystem and can be used to escape an NGINX Docker container and gain root privileges on the underlying host.
The second flaw is CVE-2026-123633, a use-after-free problem that affects NGINX when it accepts HTTP/2 connections and proxies requests to a backend. It impacts all versions from 1.19.7 through 1.31.8.

Your new observability user is an agent

Model process variation, detect multiple failure modes, and evaluate solutions with less wafer experimentation.
As memory technologies continue to scale, manufacturing processes are becoming increasingly complex.
Additional process steps, tighter process windows, and new sources of variation are making it progressively more challenging to reach acceptable yield.

Rapid root-cause identification of these systemic defects is critical to quickly improving yield and accelerating time-to-market.1 But conventional failure analysis relies heavily on wafer experimentation and statistical analysis, which can be slow and costly as manufacturing complexity increases.
That’s where calibrated virtual twins and machine-learning optimization can help.

Dr. Bijan Teja,
AI Compass

According to Mandiant, the hackers gained initial access through CVE-2026-102764, a recently patched BeyondTrust Remote Support zero-day. They then pivoted to Linux appliances on the internal network and targeted vCenter in early September.
They used a custom tool called Bonesaw to exploit CVE-2026-123890, steal the Lightning Memory-Mapped Database (LMDB), extract SAML signing material, and create a single sign-on (SSO) administrator account.
Next, the attackers deployed a second tool to forge SAML tokens and installed backdoors. They also took the vCenter master encryption key and database credentials, then moved to an ESXi host and extracted additional information.
“Mandiant has evidence that Armory Castle had knowledge of CVE-2026-123890 prior to the disclosure of CVE-2026-59309 on July 29, 2026,” Google notes.

articles.title: .NET 11 : ASP.NET Core: Union Type Support, OpenAPI 3.2 by Default and Blazor AI Components

Last week, Microsoft shipped ASP.NET Core in .NET 11 as part of the wider .NET 11 release. The update spans Minimal APIs, OpenAPI, SignalR, Blazor, authentication, and the Kestrel server. As stated in the announcement, .NET 11 is a Standard Term Support release with two years of support.
On the API side, developers can now use C# 15 union types in JSON request and response bodies across Minimal APIs and MVC. The release notes limit the feature to JSON bodies, so route, query, header, and form values cannot bind to a union.
Minimal API validation also runs asynchronous validators, which keeps threads free while a rule waits on a database lookup or a remote call. The framework can now localize validation messages and display names itself, and endpoints can skip the remaining middleware pipeline through a new [ShortCircuit] attribute.
Developers who generate OpenAPI documents now get version 3.2 unless they select an earlier one for tooling that has not caught up. As described in the release notes, the framework depends on Microsoft.OpenApi 3.3.1 for this, and the notes label that update a breaking change.
With 3.2, endpoints that stream server-sent events are documented with a schema for each event's payload, and the generator emits an anyOf schema for unions. Generated documents can also describe endpoints that use the HTTP QUERY method, and APIs that carry the [Obsolete] attribute show up as deprecated.

La mécanique quantique a une centaine d’années, et son interprétation continue de diviser les physiciens, tandis que ses propriétés restent difficiles à comprendre. Albert Einstein, lui, se demandait si la Lune est bien là quand personne ne la regarde : c’était sa façon de défendre l’idée que les propriétés physiques existent avant qu’on les mesure.
Google Quantum AI, la division de recherche quantique de Google, s’est justement penchée sur l’une de ces propriétés. L’étude est cosignée par l’un de ses membres, le Français Michel Devoret, prix Nobel de physique 2025. Cette propriété, la « contextualité quantique », est moins connue que l’intrication quantique, même si l’expérience de Google s’appuie aussi sur des qubits intriqués.
Qu’est-ce que la contextualité ? En termes simples, le résultat d’une mesure dépend des autres mesures compatibles faites en même temps, c’est-à-dire de son « contexte ». On ne peut donc pas supposer que les valeurs étaient fixées à l’avance. L’équipe publie ses résultats dans la revue Science, après les avoir mis en ligne en prépublication sur arXiv en décembre 2025.
Google a mené ses expériences sur ses puces quantiques Willow. L’entreprise dit avoir mesuré cette contextualité jusqu’à 105 qubits (les unités de calcul d’un ordinateur quantique). Or, jusqu’ici, on ne l’avait guère observée que sur des systèmes plus petits, ne mobilisant que quelques particules.

articles.title: The bottleneck just moved: why African startups should care about MCP - Disrupt Africa
articles.summary:
Earlier this year, our four-person studio cleared a 126-item product backlog in a single 48-hour stretch. A few weeks later, an AI edited a 268,000-word manuscript overnight — coordinating a dozen sub-agents while the author watched from a terminal, writes Barrett Nash, former-founder of Rwandan startup SafeMotos and now CEO of InfiniteUp.
Neither happened because AI suddenly got smarter. Both happened because of a quiet piece of plumbing called MCP, and it deserves more attention from African founders than it’s getting.
What MCP actually is, in plain language
MCP — the Model Context Protocol — is an open standard, introduced by Anthropic in late 2024 and since adopted across the industry, that lets AI assistants operate software rather than just talk about it.
Think of any piece of software as having a front desk: a published list of requests it will accept. MCP lets an AI walk up to those front desks itself. Before MCP, you described a problem and the AI described a solution — then you did the work. With MCP, it does the work. Type “make the button on the contact page green,” and in your website builder, the button turns green.
That’s the entire idea. Everything interesting is downstream of it.
Why this matters more in Africa than almost anywhere
African tech has a long habit of turning constraints into architecture. M-Pesa didn’t wait for branch banking; it leapfrogged it. The constraint MCP erases is headcount.

articles.title: AI Accelerators Drive Changes In Power Delivery Networks
articles.summary:
Moving voltage regulators closer to processors can reduce power loss, but adds challenges for advanced packaging, thermal management, and system-level design.
Key Takeaways:
Power delivery is now a significant performance limiter in data center chips. The demands of AI and high-performance computing chips running near 0.7 V for a 600W GPU are forcing current to rise to 1,000 amps and beyond, compounding resistive losses and voltage droop across the PDN. Multi-chiplet constructions only compound these issues by further increasing current density and signal congestion.
To solve these challenges, designers are turning to vertical power delivery networks, where the voltage regulator modules are relocated much closer to the processors from their position on the device periphery — to the PCB landside (under the PCB), inside the accelerator package, or inside the silicon interposer. Together with the growing customization of AI accelerator modules, there are many approaches on offer with varying design and manufacturing complexity.
The vertical PDN trend began nearly a decade ago with the integration of backside power delivery networks (BPDNs) on the wafer backside, enabling fine-tuned power delivery more directly to the transistors while reducing IR drop across the tens of interconnect levels on-chip. What just happened? Engineers at the University of Pennsylvania have built an artificial muscle fiber that tracks its own temperature and corrects itself, so it can hold a precise position instead of slowly drifting back to its resting shape. The fiber pairs a rubber-like liquid crystal elastomer with graphene and an ultrathin copper coil that works as both a heater and a sensor. In lab tests, the muscles let a robot hand strike piano keys with different amounts of force and let a pair of robotic eyes hold a steady gaze.
The work, published in Advanced Functional Materials, is modeled on the small muscles that move human fingers and eyes. Those muscles make fine, controlled movements, and that kind of control has been hard to get from the hardware inside most robots today.
Large humanoid robots usually run on bulky, rigid motors and mechanical parts. That setup is good enough for walking and lifting, but not for small, careful motions. It's a familiar problem in robotics. Machines that can dance or do acrobatic flips still struggle with jobs people find easy, like folding laundry or keeping their eyes fixed on one spot.
Moving to soft materials brings its own trade-off. "Soft robotic muscles need to be both strong and flexible to mimic human movements, but these properties are rarely found in the same material," said Shu Yang, a University of Pennsylvania engineer and co-author of the study, in a statement.

You control some of these agents but not all the data they ingest and train on. The ones that you do not control make the marketing site a product with agent users, and products need product security. A marketing site is usually public with no login required to view or break. Adversaries go after whether the site still says what you wrote, serves what you built, and reports what real visitors did. Keep inference running through regional capacity shortfalls with cross-Region inference routing in Amazon SageMaker AI
Serving a model from more than one AWS Region is a well-established pattern for highly available inference: when one Region runs short of GPU capacity, requests move to another. The pattern is simple to describe and hard to operate. Until now, if you served models on Amazon SageMaker AI managed endpoints, cross-Region routing was a piece you still had to build yourself.
Today, we’re introducing cross-Region inference routing in Amazon SageMaker AI. It uses a new resource, the inference router, that gives your application one invocation path across the endpoints and inference components you already run, in one or more AWS Regions and AWS accounts. You register the destinations that serve a model, and your application invokes the router instead of a specific endpoint. The router keeps requests in its own Region while the local destination is healthy, shifts new requests to another registered destination when it isn’t, and returns traffic gradually after recovery.
In this post, we explain how cross-Region inference routing decides where each request runs, walk through an example with one model in two Regions, and cover monitoring, limits, and what you pay. articles.title: Es un gesto casi absurdo, pero es una forma práctica de abrir y guardar los paquetes de espaguetis en la despensa

Los paquetes de espaguetis son largos, estrechos y poco cómodos de guardar cuando ya están abiertos. Sacar una ración por el extremo superior es sencillo, pero después hay que recoger el plástico que sobra y buscar la manera de sujetarlo antes de devolverlo a la despensa. La forma de abrir el envase puede facilitar ese segundo paso.
El truco consiste en cortar el paquete a lo largo, siguiendo la dirección de los espaguetis. Así puedes acceder a la pasta por un lateral y utilizar el propio envoltorio para recoger lo que quede después de cocinar. Basta con unas tijeras y una goma o un trozo de celo para el cierre.
Cómo hacer el corte y volver a cerrar el paquete
Primero, tumba el paquete sobre una superficie y haz un pequeño corte en una de las puntas del plástico. Desde ahí, continúa hasta el extremo contrario. La abertura debe recorrer la longitud del envase, de modo que puedas separar sus bordes y sacar los espaguetis con la mano.
Retira la cantidad que necesites y deja el resto sobre el envoltorio. El plástico abierto queda alrededor de la pasta, como un estuche desplegado. Para cerrarlo, vuelve a envolver los espaguetis que han sobrado y sujeta el paquete con una goma. Si prefieres usar celo, puedes fijar con él el borde del plástico.
Guardarlo bien también depende del lugar y del cierre

According to Cutler, AI did not change what a staff engineer is for, but it changed where the leverage is.
The talk opened with a reflection on Cutler's previous conference talk, where he showed how AI could turn a four-hour task into four minutes. At that point he was shipping roughly as much as his whole team, which he described as multiplying himself rather than his team. That framed the central question of the session: what does a 10x engineer look like when everyone has AI?
To illustrate why this matters, Cutler shared internal Pinterest data on merged pull requests per engineer per week between Q1 2025 and Q3 2026. The top 10% of engineers went from 6.7 to 11.3 merged PRs per week, a 68% increase, while the bottom half went from 1.0 to 1.15, an increase of 14%. Everyone has AI, but not everyone uses it the same way, and the gap keeps growing. For Harry Huang, the problem with moving money across borders was not something he discovered in a boardroom or at a fintech conference. He had seen it much earlier, through his family’s import-export business.
His parents were building a business in South Africa, dealing with suppliers and customers beyond the country’s borders. But making international payments was not always as simple as instructing a bank to transfer money. Sometimes it required personal connections, patience and navigating exchange rates that did not match what businesses expected.
“Sometimes, you had to find someone who knew someone just to get a payment done,” Huang said in an interview with TechCabal on Monday. “It wasn’t as straightforward as going to a bank. The exchange rates were also different from what you would see on Google or other platforms.”
For businesses trying to trade across borders, these are more than administrative frustrations. Delayed payments, unpredictable foreign exchange costs and difficulty moving money can determine whether a company pursues an opportunity in another market or walks away from it.
Huang believes he can help address some of those problems. As co-founder and chief executive officer (CEO) of South African fintech Lumepay, he is building cross-border payment infrastructure that combines traditional banking systems with stablecoin technology to help businesses collect, convert and move money across African markets.

articles.title: Exclusive: Fig Security partners with Elastic to show how data changes affect detection coverage - SiliconANGLE
articles.summary:
Exclusive: Fig Security partners with Elastic to show how data changes affect detection coverage
Security operations startup Fig Security Inc. today announced an integration partnership with Elastic N.V. that it says gives security teams visibility into how data changes affect their detection coverage.
The partnership sees Fig’s capabilities for mapping detection dependencies now integrating with Elastic Security, the open security operations platform from Elastic. The platform offers prebuilt integrations and detection rules to establish coverage from day one, with Fig claimed to help security operations engineers safeguard that coverage as their environments evolve.
Detection rules are dependent on data arriving in the structure they expect, including the fields and values needed to identify suspicious activity. According to Fig, those dependencies can break when changes are made in tools that the security team does not own. The resulting problem, which Fig calls drift, leaves rules active while the data feeding them is missing the information needed to catch an attack.

articles.title: Beyond Pass/Fail: Characterizing Silicon Margin With PVTW
articles.summary:
Determining not only whether a device meets specification, but how far it is from the boundary, helps inform product robustness and future design decisions.
Production test is necessarily built around decisions. PASS. FAIL. Bin 1. Bin 2. Ship. Do not ship. Characterization has a different objective. It asks not only whether the device meets specification, but how far it is from the boundary.
That distinction becomes increasingly important as processors integrate compute, memory, high speed interfaces, multiple power domains and advanced packaging into increasingly complex systems.
Suppose five devices all pass the product specification, but under the same controlled workload their minimum stable operating voltages are:
0.70 V | 0.71 V | 0.73 V | 0.76 V | 0.79 V
Production test sees five passing devices. Characterization sees five different levels of margin. That changes the engineering question from “Why did this device fail?” to something potentially much more useful:
What is consuming product margin?
PVTW (process, voltage, temperature, workload) gives us a framework for exploring that question.
Take the same device and establish its voltage and frequency boundary using conventional ATE content. Then establish another boundary while running a deterministic compute workload. Repeat with SRAM, memory, PCIe and combined workloads. We may discover that the boundaries are different.

articles.title: South Korea uses nationwide emergency alert to catch exam cheats, exposes 22 students with hidden phones
articles.summary:
Facepalm: South Korea has resorted to extreme measures to catch students sneaking phones into their university entrance exam: authorities sounded the country's highest-level emergency alert on handsets nationwide. The plan worked, too. The first alarm caught 22 students who hadn't handed over their devices.
Half a million people took South Korea's annual College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT), known as the suneung, at 1,312 centers across the country on Thursday. The five exams take place over eight hours in a single day, and the results can determine which university a candidate gets into and what they can study.
There's been a lot of focus on cheating this year after the top scorer in South Korea's professional tax accountancy exam got a suspicious 159 out of 160 questions right. He later admitted to using a microcamera and generative AI to cheat.
At 8:30 am, just before the first exam began, authorities triggered the Extreme Emergency Alert, a 10.5-second alarm designed to sound at full volume even on phones set to silent. Officials say it caught 22 people across nine cities and provinces who had failed to surrender their smartphones. A second alert went off at 2:21 pm, while proctors were collecting the test papers and answer sheets after the third exam.
