articles.title: How Amazon ECS handles blue/green, canary, and linear deployments
articles.summary:
How Amazon ECS handles blue/green, canary, and linear deployments
Deploying containers safely at scale can mean assembling your own system: traffic-splitting logic, alarm evaluation, rollback automation, approval gates. It’s infrastructure that exists solely to protect the deployment itself. AWS has built all of those capabilities directly into Amazon Elastic Container Service (ECS), so you don’t have to.
“Deploying containers safely at scale can mean assembling your own system: traffic-splitting logic, alarm evaluation, rollback automation, approval gates. It’s infrastructure that exists solely to protect the deployment itself.”
You can access all these tools through a single API endpoint. AWS built them to work out of the box when you use Amazon ECS as your container orchestration platform with the Amazon ECS deployment controller. As a result, you don’t have to build your own abstractions or learn a new framework to get the deployment behavior you want. Instead, you pick and choose the features you want through a service deployment configuration and update it as your needs change.
How the building blocks map to ECS
If you’ve run progressive delivery on Kubernetes with Argo Rollouts or Flagger, you know the shape of the stack: a controller you install and keep current, analysis wired to your metrics backend, and a traffic provider for weighted canaries. articles.title: ASUS warns of critical hard-coded key flaw in Control Center Express
articles.summary:
ASUS released Control Center Express v1.7.29 to fix three critical vulnerabilities that could let remote attackers gain administrative control of the management console and the devices it manages.
Of the three, one is a maximum-severity vulnerability (CVSS score: 10.0) tracked under CVE-2026-114202, arising from a hard-coded cryptographic key used in the product.
The flaw lets an unauthenticated remote attacker forge an authentication token and gain administrator privileges, without requiring any privileges or user interaction.
The second flaw is CVE-2026-114204, also a hard-coded key problem, which lets a remote attacker with low privileges forge a session token for a recently logged-in account.
The third is CVE-2026-114205, an authorization flaw that lets a low-privileged user create an administrator account.
ASUS Control Center Express is a central dashboard that IT administrators use to monitor and remotely manage fleets of PCs.
ASUS markets it to businesses and IT service providers and lists support for more than 200 of its business, workstation, and Corporate Stable Model motherboards.
While all three vulnerabilities are rated critical, CVE-2026-114204 has a recent-session prerequisite, and CVE-2026-114205 requires a low-privileged account, whereas CVE-2026-114202 enables remote administrative access with no prerequisites.
ASUS’s security bulletin says versions earlier than v1.7.29 are affected. However, the CVE records only list affected versions through v1.7.27, leavi…

EPFO approves systematic withdrawal plan for retiring members
Retiring members can now opt for receiving their retirement savings in periodic installments instead of a lump sum amount.
The retirement fund body Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) on Thursday approved a Systematic Withdrawal Plan (SWP) for its retiring members to receive their accumulated provident fund savings in periodic instalments instead of withdrawing the entire corpus at once.
Under the SWP, retiring members of the EPFO will receive their accumulated provident fund savings in periodic installments instead of withdrawing the entire amount at once, a Labour Ministry release said.
The decision was taken at the 240th meeting of the Central Board of Trustees (CBT) of the Employees’ Provident Fund (EPF), chaired by Union Minister for Labour & Employment and Youth Affairs & Sports, Mansukh Mandaviya.
The Board approved a proposal to introduce a Systematic Withdrawal Plan, enabling retiring EPF members to receive their accumulated provident fund savings in periodic installments instead of withdrawing the entire amount at once.
This reform will enable retiring members to withdraw their accumulated provident fund savings at regular intervals, such as monthly, quarterly or half-yearly, based on their preference.

Cheaper tokens expand adoption, and agentic workloads multiply invocations. As successful AI use cases scale, consumption can rise faster than unit prices drop. The economic question is whether the business value generated grows faster than the cost of the intelligence required to produce it. The Linux Foundation has launched the Tokenomics Foundation to develop open standards for AI cost economics, a sign that managing the economics of AI is now an industry discipline.
In this post, you will learn about six levers for optimizing token spend, how Accenture applied them in production, and how to apply them using Amazon Bedrock.
Accenture applied these levers in four client engagements across telecom, insurance, mining, and a large enterprise deployment. The same levers are available natively on Amazon Bedrock as described in this post. Where savings were measured, token spend fell by about 40–85 percent. The baseline for that fact-finding, as anyone tasked with investigating these incidents will tell you, is that the vast majority of these digital breakdowns are not the result of malicious intent but rather casualties of IT admins’ constant war to keep computer systems from collapsing under the weight of their own complexity.
“I’ve just seen enough times where we thought maybe it’s a cyberattack and it turns out it’s not. Sometimes it will be, but typically not,” says Matthew Prince, CEO of the Internet infrastructure company Cloudflare. “Right now, most of what we’re seeing is the standard background noise. Stuff breaks, and that’s just the nature of complex systems.”
So in the interest of soothing the country’s rattled nerves and helping us all find ground truth amid seemingly endless tech catastrophes, we at WIRED present our general guide to determining whether a tech outage is the result of a cyberattack. articles.title: Where should AI workloads run? Probably next to the data.

Where should AI workloads run? Probably next to the data.
AWS raised prices on EC2 Capacity Blocks, its reserved GPU capacity, by about 15% in January and about 20% in July. Picture a platform team watching a training job’s bill climb after copying a few hundred terabytes of sensor data across regions just to reach the GPUs, then realizing the data never had to move.
For AI workloads, the real question is whether the workload goes to the data or the data goes to the workload. Data gravity usually answers it.
Data gravity hits AI workloads harder than it ever hit analytics
Data gravity is the tendency of compute, applications, and services to be pulled toward large concentrations of data, because moving the data costs more than moving the logic that processes it. The larger a dataset grows, the more expensive every copy becomes, and the more everything that needs that data ends up living next to it.
Scheduled BI often tolerates periodic queries against sampled or aggregated data. Large training runs can require repeated reads of a much larger dataset, while agents retrieve fresh context throughout a workflow. When those reads cross regions or environments, transfer costs and latency add up. Each agent output also becomes new data that feeds the next round of retrieval, which compounds the pull over time.

While some users report the figure holding steady at around 20 MB, others report it writing dozens of gigabytes each day, even while idle. Klein, unsichtbar und ungewöhnlich massereich
Doch der Begleiter des Roten Riesen gibt den Forschenden Rätsel auf. Er ist sehr klein und außergewöhnlich massereich.
Das mysteriöse Objekt ist außerdem unsichtbar. Es lässt sich also nicht direkt optisch wahrnehmen, sondern nur durch die Auswirkungen seiner Schwerkraft auf die Umlaufbahn des Roten Riesen.
Ist das unsichtbare Objekt ein Neutronenstern?

Da Neutronensterne sehr klein sind, ist ihr Licht mit gängigen Instrumenten meist nicht messbar. Diese extrem dichten Objekte entstehen, wenn ein massiver Stern als Supernova explodiert.

Madrid, 2005. Un puñado de operarios tienen una misión. Dos años después, esa misión se trunca. Desaparece. Llega el abandono. Hace casi dos décadas que ni un sólo trabajador pisa el suelo de la M-203, una carretera asfaltada en parte pero conectada a ninguna parte. Ahora, la Comunidad de Madrid parece haberse tomado en serio su resurrección.
¿Qué ha pasado? La Comunidad de Madrid invertirá 61 millones de euros para culminar la carretera M-203, una vía que quedó abandonada en 2007, apenas dos años después de que dieran inicio las obras. Este anuncio ya se esperaba después de que en el verano del año pasado se pusiera sobre la mesa revivir esta carretera.
Ahora, la Comunidad de Madrid tiene precio a la vuelta de los operarios a la M-203. La intención es que con 61 millones de euros se culmine una vía alternativa para el corredor del Henares, una zona con graves problemas de tráfico. De salir adelante, sus vecinos tendrán una conexión directa entre la A-2 y la R-3.
¿M-203? Sí, así se llamó el proyecto que en 2005 arrancó de la mano de Cintra. En aquellos años se aseguró que la construcción de la vía sería posible gracias a una inversión de 78,5 millones de euros por parte de la empresa concesionaria y, a cambio, la Comunidad de Madrid le otorgaba un plazo de explotación durante 30 años.

Hair and water composition can change significantly every 100 kilometres across India, affecting how haircare products perform. It was this observation, made while researching premature greying in his 20s, that led Dhruv Sayani to build Ccigmaa Lifestyles, a Mumbai-based personal care company.
Sayani found that keratin, the protein that makes up most of human hair, responds differently to these regional variations, something he believed conventional haircare formulations did not adequately address.

articles.title: SA’s SEQFLO launches to take risk out of buying from strangers - Disrupt Africa
articles.summary:
South African startup SEQFLO has launched a digital trust platform that adds identity verification, protected payments and dispute resolution to private transactions between strangers.
Founded in Cape Town by Jarrett Booysen, SEQFLO is not a marketplace, but rather acts as a trust and transaction layer for deals that start elsewhere, whether on Facebook Marketplace, Gumtree, WhatsApp, Instagram or a seller’s own website.
Sellers create a transaction on SEQFLO and then advertise through their usual channels. Both parties are verified and agree on the terms before any money changes hands. The buyer then pays through SEQFLO, and the funds are held within the platform’s approved banking and payment structure.
Delivery or collection can be documented with photographs, and the seller is paid once the agreed conditions have been met. If something goes wrong, a structured evidence and dispute-resolution process kicks in.
“We’re not asking people to trust strangers more. We’re building SEQFLO so they don’t have to rely on trust alone,” said Booysen, who built the platform after being scammed himself.
“We constantly tell people to check a profile, ask for ID, look at proof of payment and trust their gut. But sophisticated scammers know exactly how to create those signals of legitimacy,” he said.
SEQFLO is designed to protect both sides of a deal. Buyers are covered against paying for goods that never arrive. Sellers are covered against fake proofs of payment and fraudulent buyers.

NASA recently announced a significant shakeup to the Artemis program that will land humans on the Moon.
The moves were designed to give the agency’s lunar lander providers—SpaceX with its Starship vehicle, and Blue Origin with Blue Moon—more flexibility in reaching the Moon. For Starship, this means docking with Orion in Earth orbit, and then traveling to the Moon in tandem. For Blue Moon, it shifts the rendezvous with Orion all the way to low-lunar orbit.
These changes benefit the lunar landers, but in turn impose more of a burden on the Orion spacecraft, which is built for NASA by Lockheed Martin. To understand the implications for the spacecraft, Ars spoke with Kirk Shireman, Human Spaceflight Exploration and Orion program manager at Lockheed.
Starship challenges
For Starship, the evolved plan has SpaceX fueling a Starship lunar lander in low-Earth orbit before docking with Orion in high-Earth orbit. The crew will fly to the Moon on board Orion before two of the four astronauts transfer into Starship for a landing on the Moon.
Due to the docking configuration with Starship, Orion must now fly backward to the Moon, with its Service Module at the top of the stack. This is a fundamentally different flying posture than Orion was designed for, Shireman said, and creates issues for Orion’s propulsion system.

articles.title: Mouse fight club might explain why we like to watch violent things
articles.summary:
There’s something about watching violent events that broadly appeals to us, whether it’s the latest John Wick movie, a video game, or a live UFC bout. Scientists have debated whether watching violent things could make us more aggressive, but it could also be an adaptive survival strategy. Male mice, for instance, who watched other mice fighting learned enough about how to fight to better protect themselves (compared to mice who didn’t watch fights) when pitted against stronger, more aggressive opponents, according to a paper published in the journal Nature.
The team randomly assigned male mice to three groups—fighters, spectators, or novices—and then subjected each group to eight days of training with three 10-minute sessions per day. The novices played with stuffed mice in isolation, while the spectators watched various pairs of fighter mice battle from a raised platform behind a transparent barrier—a set-up chosen to let them smell and listen to the fights as well as observe them.
The ninth day was “fight night,” when all the mice had to face a daunting opponent in three 4-minute rounds. Each fight was filmed from above so that the mouse behavior could be analyzed. To monitor corresponding changes in brain activity, the team engineered the rodents’ excitatory brain cells to glow green whenever they were activated, while inhibitory brain cells glowed red. El traspaso también afectaba a Santo Tomás, San Juan y Santa Cruz, más los islotes cercanos. Hasta ese momento eran conocidas como las Indias Occidentales Danesas.
Es importante conocer que el sistema económico de estas islas estaba basado en las plantaciones y la compraventa de esclavos. Aunque la esclavitud había sido abolida en 1848, el negocio del azúcar empezó a perder interés.
Según el Museo Nacional de Dinamarca, los barcos daneses llevaron a unas 120.000 personas esclavizadas de África al Caribe. En las islas se basaba el sistema de producción azucarera en mano de obra forzada.
En la historia del archipiélago también hay episodios de resistencia de la población esclavizada. En 1733 hubo una rebelión en San Juan. Se alzaron contra el dominio danés. En el reglamento del gobernador Philip Gardelin se detallan algunos de los castigos extremos que se practicaron.

Artificial Intelligence
Inside Amazon Connect Talent: The science of structured AI interviews
For organizations hiring hundreds or thousands of people, every interview presents the same challenge: How do you give candidates a consistent opportunity to demonstrate their skills while gathering the evidence needed to make informed hiring decisions?
Structured behavioral interviews offer a research-backed approach to this challenge. They use consistent, job-related questions and clear scoring criteria to give candidates an opportunity to demonstrate their skills. Decades of research in industrial-organizational (I-O) psychology have shown that structured interviews help organizations evaluate candidates and predict job performance (Schmidt & Hunter, 1998; Sackett et al., 2022). Yet delivering structured interviews at scale requires significant time and expertise to develop competencies, create questions, train interviewers, and evaluate responses consistently.
Amazon Connect Talent brings established hiring science to AI-led interviews at scale. Connect Talent uses structured questions, adaptive follow-ups, and evidence-based scoring to help organizations gather consistent, job-related information while giving more candidates the opportunity to demonstrate their strengths.

articles.title: DDR6 memory modules could be 44% shorter than DDR5 while delivering over 50% more bandwidth
articles.summary:
Forward-looking: JEDEC is looking forward to a point when buying DRAM doesn't require selling a kidney and DDR6 is available. In an early preview of the next-gen memory standard, the organization noted that not only would it bring several upgrades, but the proposed modules would also be around 44% shorter than DDR5 versions.
As VideoCardz notes, a full-size DDR5 stick measures just over 133 mm from end to end. The design JEDEC has in mind for DDR6 measures 74 mm, putting it within a few millimeters of those little SO-DIMMs found in laptops. Unfortunately, you can probably guess who stands to benefit most from being able to squeeze more memory into the same amount of motherboard space.
Sure enough, JEDEC singles out AI inference and agentic AI as two workloads that could use more memory close to the CPU. The speed figures it gives are for registered DIMMs, the kind typically found in servers. DDR6 RDIMMs are expected to start at 12,800 MT/s, up from the 9,200 MT/s ceiling for DDR5 RDIMMs, with 14,400 MT/s and higher speeds to follow.
That works out to a roughly 39% increase in the transfer rate right from the start. There's also the data bus, which goes from 64 bits wide to 96 bits, allowing the module to move more data with each transfer. JEDEC expects those two changes to deliver more than 50% additional bandwidth at launch. It's also developing low-power modes specifically for use in data centers.

Then, there are the AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md files and things like MCP configurations that involve some setup work that few developers will want to have to redo when something goes awry.

articles.title: "Be ready for change": AAIF’s CTO on why the agent stack won’t settle
articles.summary:
“Be ready for change”: AAIF’s CTO on why the agent stack won’t settle
If you’ve spent any time over the past year trying to get AI agents to talk to each other without tearing your architecture apart, you know the struggle: vendor lock-in, fragmented protocols, and context that definitely vanishes the second you attempt to make a cross-framework handoff.
It’s astounding how fast developers’ needs have changed just in 10 months since the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) was formed to help solve those problems.
The Linux Foundation-backed AAIF gives shared agent infrastructure a home outside any one vendor’s control. It launched in December 2025 with three projects, including the Model Context Protocol (MCP), which connects AI applications to external tools and data.
On October 22, Anthropic contributed Agent Skills, and OpenAI contributed Open Responses to the foundation, alongside projects from Hugging Face and Alibaba. The additions brought AAIF to 10 hosted projects.
The New Stack Editor-in-Chief Nick Lucchesi sat down with Manik Surtani, AAIF’s co-founder and CTO, for The New Stack podcast at AGNTCon + MCPCon in San Jose, shortly after Surtani announced the additions in his October 22 keynote. The news was still fresh — the problems behind it, though, were all too familiar.

Thursday, November 19th 2026
TSMC Reportedly Reviews Customer Finances, Asks Some Chip Buyers to Pay Upfront
TSMC is reportedly seeking to audit its customers' ability to finance chip allocations, as the company aims to secure funding for its production runs. The report states that TSMC is going as far as obtaining data on customers' financial situations, data center construction stages, and other factors that influence demand assessments. These assessments are then used to propose credit lines based on each company's balance sheet. This evaluation includes collecting information on past debt defaults, the company's position in the industry, and its liquidity. For any orders that exceed the TSMC-imposed credit limit, TSMC requires cash payments for its production runs, with some customers even needing to make upfront payments to secure production capacity. Those who cannot secure a good credit line may pre-pay their production runs to ensure allocation.
With NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang now out of the loop, TSMC is conducting checks with customers to ensure that, in the event of a broader industry shakeup, its production remains well-funded. The reported AI circular financing scheme that the entire industry has been engaging in is net positive for valuations, but TSMC wants to ensure it gets paid first, regardless of the situation. articles.title: Intel says its graphics-free D270 GPU beats Nvidia's RTX Pro 6000 by up to 5.9x in benchmarks
articles.summary:
In context: Intel first teased Crescent Island over a year ago as a data center GPU that can't even render graphics. It has none of the 3D or ray-tracing hardware you'd find on a regular graphics card; instead, the chip – now sold as the GPU D270 – spends that space on AI and scientific work. Until this week, though, Intel hadn't really shown how fast it is. That changed at the SC26 supercomputing show in Chicago.
In a post, Intel put the D270 up against Nvidia's RTX Pro 6000 Blackwell Server Edition. Instead of games or AI models, Intel went with something a little more niche. It picked four workloads that banks rely on to put a price on financial contracts.
Across those four, the D270 delivered between 1.92 and 5.9 times the performance of Nvidia's card. Its biggest win showed up in a European Monte Carlo simulation. Intel's card also did all of this at just 350W, compared to the 600W that Nvidia's card is rated for.
All four tests rely on double-precision, or FP64, calculations. Intel's Xe3P architecture handles those calculations at full speed, so the D270 barely slows down when a task needs that extra accuracy. That full-speed FP64 support is where most of the D270's lead over Nvidia's card comes from.
The RTX Pro 6000, on the other hand, uses the same chip as the GeForce RTX 5090. That silicon only handles FP64 at a tiny fraction of its usual speed, so by sticking to FP64-heavy workloads, Intel chose the kind of tests where Nvidia's card was likely to fall behind.

Artificial Intelligence
How the BMW Group governs hundreds of agents across thousands of developers
When hundreds of agents serve thousands of developers, enterprise governance can’t be an afterthought.
At the BMW Group’s R&D, more than 12,500 developers work on approximately 500 million lines of vehicle software code. This software is augmented by the BMW Connected Vehicle backend, a cloud-based system of more than 1,300 microservices providing digital services for 24 million vehicles in the field. In regulated industry, the bar for (software) quality, stability, and governance compliance is exceptionally high.
While research, frameworks, and guidelines now facilitate building agents, industrializing and operating high-quality agents in an efficient, scalable manner remains a significant challenge.
Scaling agentic AI across a large organization cannot be achieved by isolated teams. It requires collective effort, locally driven experimentation, and active knowledge sharing across the enterprise. This creates a fundamental governance dichotomy: Development teams need the freedom to innovate rapidly, while the enterprise must enforce standards for safety, security, composability, and cost-efficiency. Without that balance, organizations risk a fragmented landscape of AI islands and costly duplicate work. This presents a real challenge given hundreds of globally distributed teams building agents across the BMW Group.

articles.title: Wird GTA 6 das Gaming verändern? Wahrscheinlich kaum - aber andere Branchen dafür schon
articles.summary:
Wird GTA 6 das Gaming verändern? Wahrscheinlich kaum – aber andere Branchen dafür schon
Bei diesem Hype, diesen Wertungen und dieser Rezeption sollte man meinen, dass Gaming nach Grand Theft Auto 6 ein komplett anderes sein wird, als vorher. Und tatsächlich: GTA 6 ist natürlich ein sehr gutes Spiel. Es ist in vielen Aspekten sogar ein beeindruckendes Spiel. Aber wird es das Gaming verändern? Werden Videospiele zukünftig mehr wie GTA 6 sein? Daran kann man begründete Zweifel haben. Doch andere Branchen werden sich das Spiel wahrscheinlich genau ansehen.
Rockstars Open-World-Formel
Es gibt sie, diese Spiele, die eine Art Zäsur sind. Demon’s Souls, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, Minecraft, um nur einige zu nennen. Spiele, die Entwickler:innen und Studios beeinflusst haben. Die etwa neue Spielmechaniken einführten, Gameplay-Möglichkeiten neu ausloteten oder Genres neu definierten. Es sind Veröffentlichungen, bei denen man in der Rückschau, einige Jahre später, sehen kann: Da hat ein Wandel eingesetzt.
Grand Theft Auto war auch so ein Spiel – mit dem dritten Teil, der 2001 erschien. Dieses Spiel hat neu definiert, wie eine Open World funktioniert, und viele andere Games danach haben – mal mehr, mal weniger erfolgreich – versucht, sich dieses Muster zu eigen zu machen. Seitdem sind die Teile der GTA-Reihe aber iterativ. Sie bauen auf dem auf, was die Vorgänger schon geschaffen haben.

articles.title: Ubisoft unveils new GenAI subsidiary after laying off nearly 200 Canadians
articles.summary:
Ubisoft has founded a generative AI (GenAI) subsidiary called MotherBrain.
The company confirmed the new division alongside its latest earnings release. In the report, the French gaming giant notes that MotherBrain will serve as a “dedicated subsidiary focused on AI for gameplay innovation, supporting all game creators in developing groundbreaking experiences.” Game File first reported on the existence of MotherBrain in September.
The timing of this reveal, however, is particularly questionable, given that Ubisoft just laid off 166 employees in Quebec. That comes amid a major restructuring that has seen multiple studios close, including Ubisoft Halifax and Winnipeg, and other layoffs as part of wider cost-cutting measures. Overall, the company’s headcount dropped by about 1,100 people between April and September alone.
Meanwhile, Ubisoft has shown no signs of slowing down with GenAI. Over the past few years, the company has touted all of the ways it’s been experimenting with the technology, from background dialogue writing to an experience called Teammates that focuses on deeper interactions with NPCs.
Naturally, though, Ubisoft pushing for GenAI while axing many of its staff certainly isn’t a great look. While the company has said all of these AI endeavours are meant to support developers, not replace them, that’s always going to be a legitimate concern, especially for a company that’s looking to cut significant costs.

Blue Origin announced Thursday that its New Glenn rocket will launch data center satellites for Google in 2029 as part of that company’s Project Suncatcher program.
Google disclosed it was working on scalable orbiting data centers about a year ago and characterized the project as one of its research “moonshots.” The mission on New Glenn is designed to deploy satellites, each with computing capacity at roughly the scale of a data center rack, into Sun-synchronous orbit where they can receive nearly continuous solar energy.
“Project Suncatcher is a long-term moonshot to scale AI infrastructure in space by tapping into the abundant solar power in orbit,” said Travis Beals, senior director of Project Suncatcher at Google, in the news release. “This dedicated launch with Blue Origin represents a crucial milestone on our roadmap as we expand the boundaries of what’s possible for the future of compute.”
Catching a ride while they still can
The announcement comes as US commercial heavy lift rockets, including New Glenn, are filling up their capacity through the year 2030. The Google mission will fly on the 7×2 variant of the New Glenn rocket, the smaller version of the vehicle that has launched three times to date.

No timeframe has been provided for when a fix will be available yet, but for now, internet traffic has been rerouted to minimize the impact of the outage.

También se buscarán aquellos que aíslen mejor de las temperaturas extremas, tanto altas como bajas. Por eso, unos ingenieros han estado buscando alternativas hasta dar con una propuesta interesante: usar el material de las mantas de emergencia.
Capas apiladas de Mylar. Las mantas de emergencia están hechas con BoPET (tereftalato de polietileno orientado biaxialmente), un material conocido comercialmente como Mylar, que se obtiene estirando el PET clásico en dos direcciones. Así, se consigue una lámina mucho más fina y resistente. Pero no solo es resistente. Si se le añade aluminio, refleja muy bien la radiación infrarroja, por lo que se convierte en un aislante térmico ideal. Esa es justamente la razón por la que esta combinación se usa para fabricar mantas de emergencia, como las que se emplean para tapar a corredores de maratón tras un ejercicio extremo o a las víctimas de un accidente o desastre natural.

According to Unifor’s statement, the agreement includes wage increases that bring hourly rates to $29 by the end of the agreement, enhanced severance protections of up to 18 weeks, and an additional week of vacation for employees with 10 years of service.
For context, the organizing drive was started in 2024, and the B.C. Labour Relations Board certified Unifor Local 114 as the workers’ union in July, 2025, after finding that the logistics company started an “unnecessary hiring spree” designed to stop the certification process. The board said in its decision that the company pursued a “lengthy and pervasive anti-union campaign.”
In August, the board ordered binding arbitration, finding that Amazon’s conduct had affected the parties’ ability to reach an agreement.

articles.title: Traumatized teens sue school, cops after Doritos bag triggers AI gun alert

In October 2025, four Black high school students were sharing Cool Ranch Doritos after football practice, winding down and waiting for their rides home. It was then, in the lull of a moment any teen with after-school activities knows well, that the school’s AI gun detection system suddenly flagged one teen holding a bag of chips as a potential gunman.
Within two minutes, Baltimore County Public Schools officials who reviewed security camera footage linked to the alert determined there was no actual threat. They recognized the Doritos bag and canceled the alert, which notified not only other school officials but also the Baltimore County Police Department that no response was needed.
The false alert could have ended there—before a traumatizing campus clash with police—but it didn’t.
According to a lawsuit filed by the current and former students, Taki Allen, Yui-Osa Ogbeide, Devon Thompson Jr., and Keith Winfield III, due to “both technological and human errors,” school officials called police to the scene anyway, and the cops responded with force.

“No one told the students what they were suspected of,” the lawsuit said. “Officers separated the students, ordered them to their knees on the concrete, handcuffed them, and searched their persons and property.”

Google recently published the new "adaptive quality standards" Android developers will be required to adopt over the next few months. The change will affect apps published on the Google Play Store, with a specific focus on improving support for the latest foldable devices coming to Android.
Google said that customers are paying a premium for their cracking new foldable devices, and are consequently going to expect a similarly premium app experience. Developers will just have to adapt, or they are going to risk being demoted in Google Play's app promotion programs.
The main requirement is that apps will need to meet the "Tier 3" baseline in Android's official adaptive quality guidelines. Tier 3 apps are "adaptive ready" experiences, which means they will have to completely fill a foldable's display area without letterboxing effects or compatibility modes. Furthermore, Tier 3 apps will have to preserve text or playback state during rotation or folding, while supporting multi-window environments at the same time.

articles.title: Does your AI agent need an LLM to decide what to do next?
articles.summary:
Does your AI agent need an LLM to decide what to do next?
Say “good morning” to an AI agent, and it might search its long-term memory before saying hello back. Somewhere in that system, a service performs a semantic lookup to determine whether your greeting requires understanding your beverage preferences. Even if you take your coffee very seriously, this seems like a lot of infrastructure for two words.
Does this request need a more capable model than conventional options? Is this retrieved memory relevant? Should the workflow pause for a human?
This inefficiency and indecision is where Mike Chambers, a senior AI DevEx engineer at AWS, sees an opportunity. In a conversation last month at AGNTCon + MCPCon North America 2026 in San Jose, California, Chambers explained to The New Stack Editor-in-Chief Nick Lucchesi how developers can use decider models to handle the small judgments that add up inside an agent.
Decider models (also called decision models or System One models) are specialized AI models that choose from a fixed set of options or rate inputs on a scale — returning calibrated probabilities without generating free-form text. Popularized by TypeSafe AI’s Jev, they give software and agentic workflows fast, low-latency judgments with explicit confidence scores. (AWS’s Strands Labs released its own open-source decision model, the 2-billion-parameter Strands Decider 2B, on October 1.)

articles.title: Apache Iceberg and intelligent storage help AI reach production - SiliconANGLE

Hitachi Vantara bets smarter storage can close AI’s pilot-to-production gap
Enterprises pushing AI from pilot to production are learning that data, not GPUs, is the hardest part, and open table formats such as Apache Iceberg are part of the answer. Demand for AI infrastructure shows few signs of slowing, but much of the information companies need is still scattered, ungoverned and out of reach.
That pressure is turning storage into an active layer that classifies, governs and serves data to models. Unstructured files such as logs and medical images hold intelligence AI can now extract, according to Arun Prasad Raman (pictured, left), vice president of hybrid cloud and AI infrastructure at Hitachi Vantara Corp.
“Storage is not seen as just storing the data,” Raman said. “You need to bring in more intelligence natively rather than moving the data to another replication and bringing it back for, say, indexing. If it can do it natively, that’s where the value add is.”
Raman and Jeff Lundberg (right), principal product and solutions manager at Hitachi Vantara, spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and Gemma Allen at SC26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. In the wake of the Make America Healthy Again movement’s midterm wipeout, a top leader suggested the heavy losses came down to being outspent by wealthier, more powerful rivals. But a Stat report on MAHA’s own spending in the run-up to the election raises questions about whether the group’s priority was ever winning elections in the first place.
The dive into the financial documents reveals that the MAHA PAC, led by Tony Lyons, spent more on allies, boosters, meals, luxuries, and its affiliated nonprofit than it did on political candidates.
The findings are in stark contrast to an announcement from Lyons in the spring that he was heading a $100 million fundraiser to boost MAHA’s clout in the midterms. In reality, MAHA PAC took in $3.2 million. During the election cycle, the PAC spent more than $10.5 million, with over $7 million coming from money it had collected previously.
According to Stat’s findings, of the $10.5 million the MAHA PAC spent on the midterms, less than a tenth—roughly $1 million—went to messaging on political candidates, which are expenses called “independent expenditures.”
Andrew Mayersohn, a committees researcher at OpenSecrets, called the spending “pretty unusual,” explaining that “Major super PACs spend most of their money on independent expenditures.”

articles.title: Já há mais satélites visíveis a olho nu do que estrelas em várias regiões • Tecnoblog
articles.summary:
Já há mais satélites visíveis a olho nu do que estrelas em várias regiões
Rastros de satélites já são muito visíveis em grande parte da Europa e nos Estados Unidos.
Um estudo realizado pela empresa de engenharia Accu acende um alerta para um fenômeno cada vez mais perceptível: em muitos pontos do planeta, já há mais satélites artificiais cruzando o céu do que estrelas visíveis a olho nu. A causa é um tanto óbvia: o número crescente de satélites de órbita baixa direcionados a serviços de internet, com destaque para as unidades da Starlink.
A pesquisa foi baseada em dados levantados entre 12 e 18 de outubro deste ano. Esses dados fazem parte de um sistema de monitoramento de satélites disponibilizados pela Força Espacial dos Estados Unidos no site CelesTrak.
No período em questão, os pesquisadores da Accu analisaram as trajetórias de 15.833 satélites artificiais que operam em órbita baixa — em linhas gerais, aqueles que estão a até 2.000 km de altitude.
O estudo constatou que, em média, 710 satélites atravessavam o céu de uma cidade britânica de latitude intermediária à noite, considerando o horizonte completamente desobstruído. Destes, uma média de 105 satélites poderiam ser vistos a olho nu porque estavam refletindo a luz do Sol, brilhando tanto ou mais do que as estrelas.
Este é, de fato, um ponto de atenção, pois satélites artificiais não emitem luz própria. Eles podem ser notados à noite, ao entardecer ou ao amanhecer porque refletem a luz solar.

articles.title: Nvidia se enfrenta a una nueva amenaza tras la destitución de Jensen Huang: la pérdida de sus mejores ingenieros
articles.summary:
Por primera vez desde que Jensen Huang dejó de ser su CEO, Nvidia reunió a sus empleados en Santa Clara para darles un mensaje: nadie debe preocuparse por su sueldo. Aunque el hombre que hizo millonarios a muchos de esos empleados ya no esté al frente de la compañía no hay motivos para marcharse.
Al parecer, la salida de Huang no solo ha traído a una nueva CEO interina, sino que también se ha convertido en un incremento salarial para evitar que los mejores ingenieros de la empresa sigan a su cofundador en su próxima aventura laboral.
Dinero antes de lo previsto. Colette Kress, CEO interina designada por el consejo de administración de Nvidia para cubrir la dimisión de Jensen Huang tras sus 'affaires' extramatrimoniales y las sospechas de espionaje de una de sus amantes, prometió subidas de sueldo y más acciones para sus empleados.
El anuncio se hizo durante la presentación de resultados de la compañía para el tercer trimestre fiscal, y llegarán mucho antes del ciclo habitual. Nvidia presentó unos ingresos de 115.800 millones de dólares en el tercer trimestre, un 103% más que hace un año. Un analista de Bank of America preguntó a Kress por la retención de talento, a lo que la directiva respondió que estabilizar la plantilla era "probablemente lo más importante" y que lo mejor que pueden hacer es "cuidar de cada uno de los empleados".
La acción de Nvidia subió cerca de un 5% al día siguiente.

articles.title: NVIDIA : des résultats étincelants... et pourtant une action qui recule
articles.summary:
Les résultats du troisième trimestre de l'exercice actuelle de NVIDIA ont été exceptionnels. Et pourtant, le marché a encore sanctionné l'ex-firme de Jensen Huang !
Les temps sont difficiles du côté de NVIDIA. Et ce, évidemment, du fait de la très grave polémique qui a entraîné finalement la démission de Jensen Huang. Et depuis, même si l'activité est toujours brillante au sein de l'entreprise, elle crée un vrai mouvement de défiance au sein des marchés. Ce qui se confirme encore cette semaine, avec une situation franchement paradoxale.
Des résultats brillants, au-dessus même des attentes des analystes
NVIDIA a encore présenté des résultats étincelants cette semaine pour le troisième trimestre de son exercice. Son chiffre d'affaires a ainsi crû, durant le troisième trimestre de l'exercice actuel, de +103%, à 115,8 milliards de dollars.
Une croissance tout simplement folle, et qui a même dépassé les attentes des analystes, qui voyaient plutôt NVIDIA annoncer un chiffre d'affaires trimestriel de 108,85 milliards de dollars. Et pourtant, le marché n'a pas connu d'embellie derrière.
Un cours à la Bourse qui réagit négativement
En effet, ces résultats présentés mardi soir, après la clôture de la Bourse, n'ont pas eu l'effet que l'on aurait attendu. Ils ont d'abord fait bondir le cours de 2% à l'ouverture mercredi, à 159,19 dollars, pour dégringoler dans la journée, et clôturer à environ 150 dollars.

articles.title: Raptor chip stacks 3D DRAM to tackle inference memory limits - SiliconANGLE
articles.summary:
D-Matrix bets stacked DRAM can solve inference’s memory bandwidth problem
As artificial intelligence workloads shift to inference, memory bandwidth decides whether hardware generates tokens quickly or sits idle. D-Matrix Corp. is answering with Raptor, a second-generation chip stacking 3D DRAM beneath its compute logic.
AI infrastructure has become a systems game, and winners combine memory, interconnect and software into cohesive designs, according to Satyam Srivastava (pictured), fellow at d-Matrix.
“It’s no longer a chip problem. Chip plays a part of it. Memory bandwidth is a fundamental advantage that has to be solved,” Srivastava said. “The next is energy efficiency. The next is interconnect efficiency. The next is software cohesiveness.”
Srivastava spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier at SC26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed d-Matrix’s Raptor chip and its stacked 3D DRAM, inference memory bandwidth and the shift toward heterogeneous computing. (* Disclosure below.)
Raptor brings a stacked-memory tier to inference
D-Matrix proves each risky technology on a test chip first. Jayhawk proved die-to-die connectivity, and Jayhawk II validated digital in-memory computing. The Corsair accelerator combined both and entered full production earlier this year, Srivastava explained.

articles.title: Is AI becoming feral?
articles.summary:
Is AI becoming feral?
Oxford experts make the case for thinking of AI as ‘feral’
“A horde of AI agents conspired against their creators,” cried a recent headline of an article published in The Economist.
“‘We’re plausibly close to crossing the line’: are warnings of uncontrollable AI coming true?” the Guardian asked just a few days later.
These are just some of the many alarming front-page news stories which have emerged after an autonomous AI agent in Open AI’s training recently breached Hugging Face, an American company based in New York City that develops computation tools for building applications using machine learning.
However, despite what these headlines suggest, the future is not necessarily doomed. As our Oxford colleague Ciaran Martin recently wrote in the Economist, “fears of AI-induced cyber-Armageddon are overdone”.
Jerome Ravetz, Affiliate of the Institute for Science, Innovation and Society (InSIS), University of Oxford; Lukas Zumbrunn, Oxford-Hyundai Motor Group Foresight Centre, Saïd Business School, University of Oxford; Rafael Ramirez, Oxford-Hyundai Motor Group Foresight Centre, Saïd Business School, University of Oxford
Still, it’s true that the unprecedented way in which AI agents have coordinated and communicated raises novel, radical uncertainties. How concerned should we be? articles.title: Amazon fights the Delivery Protection Act with homepage banner, in-app pop-up
articles.summary:
In an unprecedented move, Amazon is using its app and website to try to convince shoppers to not support a New York City bill.
When I log into Amazon today, I’m met with a vertical banner that reads: “ATTENTION NYC Council could add up to $5 per order” with a button that says “Act now.”
I also saw a smaller version of the notice on an order confirmation page on Amazon’s website. The message is delivered as a pop-up for users of the Amazon app, Bloomberg reported. Amazon hasn’t specified whether the messaging targets NYC residents based on addresses saved in their Amazon account or uses other techniques, such as device location services, but I only see the banner if I’m logged into Amazon.
Amazon is referring to Introduction 0518-2026 ( 518), also known as the Delivery Protection Act. If passed, it would require Amazon to directly employ the third-party delivery contractors that it uses.
Clicking on “Act now” on Amazon’s homepage or in the app brings up a page that gives shoppers a way to contact their NYC Council member and further states:
Right now, Amazon works with a network of small delivery businesses that are deeply embedded in your communities. If this legislation passes, we’d no longer be able to work with them, and we’d be forced to consider moving our operations outside of the city. That would likely mean slower and more expensive delivery for millions of customers in New York City, while also threatening small businesses and their thousands of employees.

articles.title: China's first fully AI-generated movie flops at the box office
articles.summary:
No AI in Cinemas: China's first fully AI-generated film has flopped at the box office. The country is at the forefront of AI adoption across both businesses and society, but consumers are apparently unwilling to pay for what many might consider genAI "slop."
Sanxingdui: Future Past, a 100-minute sci-fi movie about a future AI apocalypse, failed to earn enough at the box office to cover the AI token costs required to generate the entire film. China's first fully AI-generated feature film has turned into a massive flop, despite locals already spending countless hours watching AI-generated clips on their smartphones.
According to box office figures tracked by Beacon Pro, Sanxingdui "generated" just around 1.8 million yuan ($270,000) after spending three weeks in Chinese cinemas. Meanwhile, the team behind the film reportedly had tens of millions of yuan in production costs to recoup before turning a profit.
Bona Film Group, the company behind the movie, adopted an entirely AI-based workflow, without actors, performers, or other cinema professionals. Yue Ming, the director and writer behind Sanxingdui's convoluted plot, worked with Shengshu Technology and its Vidu AI platform to complete the project. The team first generated a large number of clips before assembling the final "movie" by stitching the individual visuals together.
Unsurprisingly, the resulting genAI patchwork made for a disjointed story that very few moviegoers bothered to watch in theaters. According to University…

articles.title: Guerre contre l’IPTV : l’un des plus gros sites pirates de Turquie ferme ses portes
articles.summary:
Un nouveau géant du piratage vient de tomber. L’Alliance for Creativity and Entertainment (ACE) a annoncé la fermeture définitive de Dizigom, l’un des plus importants sites de streaming illégal de Turquie. La plateforme, qui comptait environ 21 millions de visites par mois, permettait de regarder gratuitement des films et des séries. Pour rappel, l’ACE est une coalition internationale qui réunit plus de 50 grands groupes de l’industrie du divertissement, dont Amazon, Apple TV, Netflix, Paramount, Sony Pictures, Universal, Disney et Warner Bros. Discovery.
À lire aussi : Un géant de l’IPTV pirate indien cesse ses activités
Trois ans d’enquête pour faire tomber Dizigom
La coalition a ouvert une enquête sur Dizigom dès 2023. Avec l’aide de la police et la justice de la Turquie, elle a cherché à identifier tous les responsables du site, à débusquer leurs biens et à cartographier l’infrastructure technique du service. Les investigations ont fini par porter leurs fruits.
Face aux poursuites pénales brandies par l’ACE, les pirates à l’origine de Dizigom ont fini par accepter un accord à l’amiable. Ils se sont engagés à fermer définitivement le service et à céder 16 noms de domaine à l’ACE. Désormais, toutes les adresses du site renvoient vers une page qui présente les dangers du piratage et fait la liste des offres de streaming légales.

Rockstar et Take-Two n’ont pas commenté la disparition du site. Et l’hypothèse selon laquelle le portage aurait été réalisé à partir de code source ayant fuité n’a pas été confirmée.

articles.title: Power-efficient inference chips let enterprises own AI hardware - SiliconANGLE
articles.summary:
AI inference servers shrink to fit the air-cooled racks enterprises already run
Power-efficient inference chips are becoming the entry price for enterprises that want to run AI on hardware they own.
As AI shifts from building models to running them every day, costly graphics processing unit racks and the liquid cooling they demand keep many companies renting compute instead. That gap is opening room for challengers to the incumbent chipmakers. Axelera AI B.V. built its business at the edge with low-power chips and edge AI development tools, and it is now taking that technology into data center infrastructure, according to Manuel Botija (pictured), vice president and head of product at Axelera.
“Enterprises cannot own their own infrastructure. They’re locked out because of the cost and the power,” Botija said. “We are enabling them now to own it. It’s not that we are helping the world save power or save money — which we are — but it’s that we are unlocking use cases that were simply not possible before.”
Botija spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and Rebecca Knight at SC26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. Aside from that, it’s also tracking 93 large “AI factories” that are either under construction or being expanded via satellite imagery. This massive power consumption is one of the reasons for the opposition against their construction in communities, with residents blaming them for increased utility prices. Enterprise adoption of artificial intelligence is creating new requirements for enterprise AI infrastructure. While much of the early AI investment centered on access to powerful GPUs, organizations moving AI applications and agents into production are discovering that accelerators are only one part of the equation.
Agentic AI systems need environments where they can execute code, access data, connect to enterprise applications and operate securely across distributed infrastructure. That requires more than bare-metal GPU capacity. It calls for a complete cloud platform that combines compute, networking, storage, security and the services needed to manage applications at scale.
That shift is creating an opportunity for neocloud providers, but it is also changing what enterprises expect from them. Infrastructure providers increasingly need to support the full application lifecycle rather than simply supply specialized hardware.

Pulitano, profesor de la Universidad de Sídney, dijo a MIT Technology Review que el sistema funciona como “un cuerpo artificial”. Se llama Sistema de Perfusión de Órganos Extendida (Extended Organ Perfusion System) y combina bombas automáticas y sensores que aportan nutrientes y sangre y retiran los desechos. El hígado se mantuvo a temperatura corporal, unos 37 °C (98,6 °F).
Un resumen científico del equipo, publicado en el programa del congreso de trasplantes TTS 2026, da cifras más precisas. Con el sistema se conectaron ocho hígados donados enteros, después de otros ocho usados para desarrollar el método. Todos se recuperaron del daño inicial en 24 a 48 horas y el que más duró llegó a 47 días.
Según el mismo resumen, el análisis del tejido mostró que el órgano conservó su estructura, aunque en sus células se formaron mitocondrias gigantes, las estructuras que producen la energía celular.

Medical AI startup Boltz raises $110M to speed up small molecule research
Boltz PBC, a startup that develops artificial intelligence models for pharmaceutical researchers, has raised $110 million in funding.
Bessemer led the Series A investment. Boltz stated on Wednesday that the fund was joined by a large group of new and returning backers. The consortium included Greycroft, Andreessen Horowitz, Amplify Partners, F-Prime Capital, Hummingbird and others.
Small molecules, the building blocks of many drugs, can only neutralize a pathogen after binding to it. As a result, researchers start drug discovery projects by looking for molecules that have a high binding affinity with pathogens. They often review hundreds of thousands of candidate molecules per project. The process can take months and often costs millions of dollars.
Boltz offers an AI model called BoltzMol-1 that speeds up the workflow. It generates binding affinity data by reviewing only a few dozen, particularly promising molecules instead of the hundreds of thousands usually needed. The fewer molecules need to be studied, the less time the analysis takes.
Binding affinity evaluations don’t yield drug discoveries right away. Instead, they produce data points called small molecule hits. Those are essentially faint clues that help researchers pinpoint the area where they should focus their efforts.

Google passe de l’incitation à l’obligation. Depuis Android 12L, en 2022, la firme encourageait les développeurs à adapter leurs applications aux grands écrans, mais Sammobile juge que la progression est restée trop lente. Le lancement de l’iPhone Duo, a servi de déclencheur : Google ne veut plus laisser les éditeurs avancer à leur rythme.
Un plancher « Tier 3 » imposé dès avril 2027
Le dispositif repose sur trois niveaux de qualité adaptative. Le Tier 3, « Adaptive ready », est le seul obligatoire : l’application doit occuper tout l’écran sans bandes noires ni mode de compatibilité, fonctionner en multifenêtre et conserver son état (position de défilement, texte saisi, lecture vidéo) lors d’un pliage, d’une rotation ou d'un redimensionnement.
Les sanctions sont nettes : une application hors des clous ne pourra plus être publiée ni recevoir de mise à jour, et pourrait perdre en visibilité. Les applications existantes non mises à jour resteront toutefois téléchargeables. Le couperet touche donc surtout les éditeurs actifs, pas le catalogue dormant.

Intuit sells Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for $3.68B, less than a third of what it paid
Financial software company Intuit Inc. today announced that it has agreed to sell its Mailchimp email marketing business to Italian technology holding company Bending Spoons S.p.A. for about $3.68 billion.
Coming five years after Intuit agreed to acquire Mailchimp for $12 billion, the sale price is less than a third of what the company paid. The 2021 purchase was the largest in Intuit’s history at the time.
Although Bending Spoons describes the transaction as all-cash, Intuit will reinvest $368 million of its proceeds in newly issued Bending Spoons shares. That leaves Intuit with $3.31 billion in cash from the sale, according to the companies. Included in the deal is The Rocket Science Group LLC, the legal entity behind Mailchimp. Closing is expected in early 2027, subject to regulatory approvals.
Selling Mailchimp is said to sharpen Intuit’s focus on the artificial intelligence-native tools it has built to help businesses win new customers, manage their pipeline and grow. Once the deal closes, Intuit intends to use the cash proceeds to buy back its own shares before the end of fiscal 2027.
Jack Tam, a senior vice president at Intuit, said the company is confident Bending Spoons “will lead Mailchimp to continued success in this next chapter.”

articles.title: Una estrella de Andrómeda se zampó a su vecina. Detectarlo fue como buscar el agua de un cubo en el mar
articles.summary:
Cuando las estrellas envejecen, su envoltura se hincha hasta el punto de engullir buena parte de la materia que les rodea. Por ejemplo, si una gigante roja tiene una estrella compañera, podría devorarla por el camino. Es algo que se cree desde hace mucho tiempo. Sin embargo, los científicos no han logrado captar este proceso de principio a fin. Al menos hasta ahora. Y es que, recientemente, un equipo de astrónomos dirigido desde la Universidad de Columbia acaba de describir el que podría ser el primer evento de este tipo detectado por los telescopios. Es cierto que no se puede afirmar con seguridad, pero son muchas las pistas que apuntan a ello.
Siete años de seguimiento. Todo comenzó con la observación de AT 2025abao, una gigante roja de 7 masas solares, ubicada en la galaxia de Andrómeda, a 2,5 millones de años luz de la Tierra. En 2023, dos telescopios de infrarrojos, NEOWISE y WINTER, detectaron que esta estrella había aumentado su luminosidad. El primero es un telescopio espacial y el segundo un telescopio terrestre. Por lo tanto, había dos rastreos independientes en los que se detectó la misma señal. Esto descartaba un posible error instrumental. Además, cuando los científicos analizaron registros anteriores, comprobaron que ese aumento de luminosidad había empezado en 2018, pero nadie se había dado cuenta.

articles.title: Wiz ties Microsoft Agent Framework package compromise to release pipeline certificate - SiliconANGLE

Wiz ties Microsoft Agent Framework package compromise to release pipeline certificate
Microsoft Corp.’s official Python package for its Agent Framework artificial intelligence agent toolkit was compromised earlier this week, as an attacker published two malicious versions to the Python Package Index that were designed to steal cloud and developer credentials.
The malicious versions, 1.26.1 and 1.26.2, were published on Tuesday through Microsoft’s own publisher account, giving them the appearance of a routine update to a package that sees close to 200,000 downloads a month. Both versions were pulled from PyPI within about an hour, but anyone who installed them in that window is at risk.
Researchers at cloud security company Wiz Inc. have since found that the attacker appears to have gained publishing access using a client certificate and private key for Microsoft’s Engineering System Release Pipeline, an internal service the company uses to sign and publish packages. Address filtering on the service blocked the attacker’s first attempt from Amazon Web Services, according to Wiz, though the attacker was able to publish on a second try from Microsoft-owned address space.
How the attacker obtained the credentials is not known. Microsoft had not responded to a request for comment from BleepingComputer as of Wednesday.

Incident remediation company Resolve AI Inc. has announced the launch of SRE-1, a new model that has been trained to find the root cause of production alerts, and Primary On-call, a new service that puts its artificial intelligence agents on call ahead of human engineers.
The new model, announced Wednesday, reflects the company’s argument that while AI has transformed how software gets written, it has barely touched how software gets run. According to Resolve AI, production has no public training corpus to match the published code that models learned from, as incidents at each company stay private.
SRE-1 is a 27 billion-parameter model built on open weights and trained by a team of 16 AI researchers over a final run of 7.4 days on up to 512 graphics processing units. Measured on the same incidents before and after training, which used reinforcement learning alone, the pass rate for a single investigation rose from 6.9% to 38.8%.
Resolve AI used Snowflake Inc.’s Cortex Training, a serverless service for customizing open-weight models, to build SRE-1. Snowflake Senior Vice President of Engineering Vivek Raghunathan said Resolve AI was the first design partner for the service.

TSMC plans to begin mass production of its N2X node in 2027, meaning "Olympic Ridge" will likely arrive a few months later, with Computex 2027 being the probable announcement date.
AMD likely chose the N2X node for its higher clock potential. Originally, TSMC targeted HPC workloads, but desktop processors can also benefit from high clock speeds for maximum performance. Los televisores inteligentes recopilan datos constantemente sobre lo que sus dueños miran, sin que la mayoría lo note. La tecnología detrás de esta vigilancia tiene nombre: Reconocimiento Automático de Contenido, conocido por sus siglas en inglés como ACR.
El ACR identifica prácticamente cualquier cosa que aparezca en pantalla: contenido de aplicaciones propias del televisor, canales de televisión abierta, consolas y dispositivos conectados por HDMI. Para lograrlo, genera una huella digital de lo que se reproduce y la compara con bases de datos hasta reconocer el programa o la escena exacta.
Qué es el ACR y por qué preocupa
Es una función integrada en el hardware de la mayoría de los televisores inteligentes que captura audio y capturas de pantalla cada pocos segundos para identificar el contenido visualizado. Esa información se envía al fabricante, que la usa para construir perfiles de consumo y vender publicidad dirigida.
Según la compañía de ciberseguridad Kaspersky, algunas funciones del televisor podrían ser aprovechadas por personas no autorizadas si el dispositivo no está correctamente protegido. Por su parte, Proton señala que esta recopilación suele quedar oculta entre los ajustes del equipo o viene activada de fábrica, lo que hace que muchos usuarios la acepten sin saberlo al configurar el televisor por primera vez.

Google publicó este jueves en la revista Science un experimento con un juego que, por una razón matemática, nadie puede ganar siempre. Su chip cuántico Willow acertó el 98,3% de las veces. Con cualquier método tradicional, el máximo posible es el 88,9%.
El dato importa por lo que prueba. Pasar ese límite solo es posible si la máquina funciona con las reglas de la física cuántica. El juego sirve entonces como examen: muestra si un chip es cuántico en los hechos, y cuánto.
Entre los autores figura el premio Nobel de Física 2025 Michel Devoret. El trabajo circulaba desde diciembre de 2025 como borrador en arXiv, el archivo en línea donde los físicos comparten sus resultados antes de que otros científicos los revisen.
Un acertijo que se puede probar en casa
El punto de partida es un acertijo. Hay que dibujar una cuadrícula de tres por tres y llenar cada casilla con +1 o -1. Los números de cada fila, multiplicados, tienen que dar +1. Los de cada columna, -1.
No tiene solución. Las filas exigen que en toda la cuadrícula haya una cantidad par de -1, y las columnas, una cantidad impar. Las dos cosas no pueden ser ciertas a la vez.
“Parece un juego de sudoku. ¡Inténtenlo! Es imposible de hacer”, desafió Rodrigo Cortiñas, investigador vinculado a Google Quantum AI y al Yale Quantum Institute, especializado en información cuántica, física atómica y circuitos superconductores, en diálogo con Infobae. articles.title: EID eSIM : ce numéro à 32 chiffres caché dans votre smartphone, à quoi sert-il vraiment ?

EID eSIM : à quoi sert cet identifiant et où le trouver sur son smartphone ?
EID eSIM : découvrez à quoi sert cet identifiant à 32 chiffres, sa différence avec l’IMEI et comment le trouver sur iPhone ou Android. Lisez le guide.
L’EID (Embedded Identity Document) est le numéro de série unique à 32 chiffres gravé dans la puce eUICC de votre smartphone, indispensable pour que votre opérateur ou des fournisseurs d’eSIM de voyage comme Ubigi, Holafly ou GoMoWorld puissent y télécharger et activer à distance votre forfait mobile. Ce guide explique son rôle, le distingue de l’IMEI, de l’ICCID et du numéro de téléphone, puis indique où le retrouver sur iPhone et Android.
| Identifiant | Signification exacte | Longueur / Format | Élément identifié | Rôle principal dans le réseau | 
|---|---|---|---|---|

articles.title: NAND Spot Prices Slide 20% in Weeks as Consumer Demand Dries Up
articles.summary:
Thursday, November 19th 2026
NAND Spot Prices Slide 20% in Weeks as Consumer Demand Dries Up
NAND flash appears to be finally getting cheaper, at least on the spot market. According to the Seoul Economic Daily, spot prices for NAND flash have dropped roughly 20% since the second half of October. TrendForce says the drop in price took just two weeks, as Chinese traders dumped inventory. A 512 Gb wafer now goes for about $14.30, which is 32% below last quarter, and 1 Tb products are down 19% to $24.90. Apparently, the reasoning is weak consumer demand, since buyers are now delaying upgrades due to high prices. Moreover, phone manufacturers are trimming base storage specs, and PC makers are selling through their existing stock as shipments continue to fall.
That's the spot side of the story, but contract prices run on long-term deals and have been slower to react. Bank of America reportedly expects smartphone and PC NAND contract prices to fall 5-10% QoQ in Q1 2027, while enterprise products are expected to hold flat or slightly creep up. TrendForce also expects overall NAND contract prices to slip 0-5% in Q2 2027. In light of all these predictions, it looks like there is some relief on the horizon as far as NAND prices go. That's a turnaround from early reports that predicted the shortage would last at least three more years. However, now it looks like SSD prices will continue to fall slowly but surely into 2027, at least on the consumer side.

"These releases are part of PHP's regular four-week release cycle and will address security vulnerabilities affecting all supported PHP versions," the maintainers said. "The highest severity is CRITICAL."

The update is expected to include CVE-2026-115560, a remote code execution flaw that succeeds only if the following conditions are met -
- An application sets session.serialize_handler to php_binary or php_serialize in its configuration, and its code switches the handler to php with ini_set() before calling session_start().
- Session upload progress is enabled, which is PHP's default.
As mitigations, users were urged to set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 until the next regular bugfix release and restart the PHP worker for the setting to be applied.
The development comes nearly a month after PHP released fixes for two critical vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, collectively tracked as PHP2Shell that enable unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE) via specially crafted HTTP requests.

articles.title: Qué tan efectivo es cargar el celular en modo avión para llegar al 100%
articles.summary:
Cargar el celular en modo avión puede acelerar el proceso para llegar al 100%. Según la empresa española Yup Charge, activar esta función durante la carga puede reducir hasta un 25% el tiempo necesario, porque el dispositivo deja de destinar energía a mantener activas las conexiones de WiFi, datos móviles y Bluetooth.
Cuando el teléfono opera en modo normal, sus radios de comunicación trabajan de forma continua en segundo plano y consumen energía que compite con la que entra por el cargador.
Al desactivar esas funciones con el modo avión, una mayor parte de la corriente disponible se destina a reponer la batería. El resultado es una carga más rápida, sin necesidad de comprar accesorios adicionales.
Por qué el modo avión acelera la carga
El modo avión desactiva las antenas de radio, suspende las notificaciones y detiene la sincronización de aplicaciones. Según Yup Charge, esto permite que una mayor proporción de la corriente se dirija a las celdas de la batería, lo que explica la diferencia de velocidad.

Uber lanzó una prueba piloto llamada Uber Kids, que permite a los padres pedir viajes para niños de 10 a 12 años. El servicio funciona desde esta semana en Austin, Nashville y Madison, en Estados Unidos, según informó la empresa y confirmaron Bloomberg y Business Insider.
Hasta ahora, los pasajeros más jóvenes que Uber transportaba sin un adulto a bordo eran adolescentes, según Business Insider. En las opciones habituales, como UberX, los menores de 10 a 12 años no pueden viajar solos, indica la página oficial del servicio.
La empresa lo describe como un programa limitado. Los niños solo viajan con conductores de buena calificación, con antecedentes verificados y con un curso obligatorio sobre este servicio, según Uber.
Un adulto en la recogida y un código para arrancar
Solo el adulto vinculado al perfil del niño puede pedir el viaje y cambiar el destino. El niño no necesita cuenta ni aplicación propia: recibe los datos del viaje por mensaje de texto al número que el padre registra.
Un adulto autorizado debe estar con el niño en el momento de la recogida. Puede ser el padre u otra persona designada en la aplicación. Ese adulto entrega al conductor un código personal, y sin ese código el viaje no comienza.
Los viajes deben ser directos y de una sola parada. El conductor no puede cancelarlos a mitad de camino ni dejar al niño lejos del destino fijado. Uber exige notas de bajada y recomienda que un adulto espere al niño al llegar.

articles.title: Intel claims CPU top spot for the first time for over a year — now can it stay there as AMD fights back?
articles.summary:
Intel claims CPU top spot for the first time for over a year — now can it stay there as AMD fights back?
Intel took an impressive five points of desktop CPU share from AMD
- Mercury Research says Intel gained overall x86 unit share in Q3 2026 for the first time since Q2 2025, reaching 69.9%
- The gain came almost entirely from desktops (Intel up about five points to 70.1%), while AMD set records in the mobile (29.2%) and server (35.5%) segments
- Both firms, however, have guided client revenue down more than 20% in Q4 as memory prices squeeze PCs, and AMD's Q4 revenue guide sits entirely above Intel's
Intel has clawed back overall x86 CPU market share from AMD for the first time since the second quarter of 2025, according to new Mercury Research figures, but the gain rests on a single segment, a single quarter, and a PC market that both companies now expect to shrink sharply.
Intel's share of x86 processor unit shipments, excluding embedded and semi-custom chips, rose to 69.9% in Q3 2026, while AMD's slipped to 30.1%, according to Tom's Hardware.
The move is small but interesting: AMD's sequential decline was stated at 0.6 percentage points, but once IoT and semi-custom SoCs are counted, Intel's lead grew by just 0.2 points to 66.1%, according to HotHardware, even as Intel remains 4.5% down overall on a yearly basis from a 74.5% share of the market.

Apple recrute pour construire un agent d’intelligence artificielle capable de naviguer sur le web, d’utiliser vos applications et d’écrire du code à votre place, selon Bloomberg. La firme de Cupertino envisagerait un lancement fin 2027, alors qu’elle complique l’accès des agents concurrents au Mac.
« Imaginez un agent IA capable d’utiliser un ordinateur à la manière d’une personne compétente. Il navigue sur le web, passe d’une application à l’autre, exécute des commandes, écrit et corrige du code, et fait appel à des services », écrit Apple dans une offre d’emploi repérée par Bloomberg. La marque à la pomme recrutait le responsable d’une équipe « Agentic AI – Proactive », et l’annonce a disparu de son site peu après, d’après Digital Trends. Selon Bloomberg, le projet démarre à peine. Google vient d’ouvrir à Gemini le contrôle du Mac, une possibilité offerte par ChatGPT et par Muse, l’agent IA de Meta.
L’agent d’Apple enchaînerait seul des tâches entre plusieurs applications
D’après l’offre, l’équipe travaille sur des agents qui « planifient et réalisent des tâches en plusieurs étapes » dans les applications, le navigateur, la ligne de commande et le code. Ils pourront répartir le travail entre des sous-agents spécialisés, c’est-à-dire d’autres IA chargées chacune d’une partie de la mission. Muchas aplicaciones de streaming no oficiales no están disponibles en tiendas como Google Play Store o App Store, por lo que los usuarios deben descargarlas desde sitios web alternativos.
Esas páginas pueden evitar los controles de calidad y seguridad de las tiendas oficiales y facilitar la distribución de software malicioso.

articles.title: Today I learned 21 humanoid robots ran a half marathon alongside humans
articles.summary:
Today I learned 21 humanoid robots ran a half marathon alongside humans
In one year, robot runners went from stumbling to record-breaking
On April 19, 2025, 21 humanoid robots lined up next to roughly 12,000 human runners at the Beijing E-Town half marathon. It was the first time robots had raced alongside people over a 21km course, Reuters reported, though the machines ran in their own separate lane.
Things didn't go great for the robots. Only six robots made it to the finish line. Even the winner needed more than twice as long as the fastest human. But they made a shocking comeback in the next year's rematch.
A messy first race
According to the rules, teams could swap batteries mid-race and bring in a substitute robot for a time penalty, confirm several reports. The course didn't make things easy, though. Robots had to handle slopes of up to 9 degrees and 14 turns.
Most of the robots were remote-controlled by operators jogging beside them. But the winner took a different approach by following a human pacer who wore a signaling device on his back.
The winner was Tiangong Ultra, a 1.8-meter-tall robot from the Beijing Humanoid Robot Innovation Center. It crossed the line in 2 hours, 40 minutes and 42 seconds, while the men's race winner finished in about 1 hour and 2 minutes.
Tiangong Ultra needed three battery changes along the way. The center's CTO, Tang Jian, credited its long legs and an algorithm that imitates how humans run marathons. Second place went to Noetix Robotic…

articles.title: Fibre en campagne : pourquoi les élus préparent un recours contre l’Arcep
articles.summary:
Les élus locaux reprochent à l’Arcep de laisser aux opérateurs commerciaux le dernier mot sur le financement de la fibre à la campagne. Quatre associations réclament le retrait de son projet tarifaire, et deux d’entre elles annoncent un recours devant le Conseil d’État.
Si vous habitez à la campagne, votre fibre passe le plus souvent par un réseau d’initiative publique (RIP), construit par les collectivités locales. Ces réseaux couvrent près de 70 % du territoire et plus de 40 % de la population. Orange, SFR, Bouygues Telecom et Free louent leurs lignes chaque mois pour vendre leurs abonnements, à des tarifs fixés dans des contrats vieux d’une dizaine d’années. Le 15 octobre dernier, l’Arcep a calculé qu’un peu plus de la moitié de ces réseaux facturent moins que le coût de leur entretien, avec un écart de 0,50 à 2 euros par ligne et par mois sur la plupart d’entre eux. Pour combler ce manque, le régulateur recommande de renégocier les contrats, sans obliger les opérateurs commerciaux à accepter. Et en bout de ligne, les élus des collectivités locales et territoriales, qui ne sont pas forcément d'accord avec la note.

articles.title: Congreso de EE.UU. revela que ChatGPT, Claude y Grok generaron planes de ataques en 12 horas
articles.summary:
La Oficina de Responsabilidad Gubernamental (GAO), el organismo de control del Congreso de Estados Unidos, identigicó que ChatGPT, Claude y Grok generó información viable para planear atentados con explosivos y ataques a la red eléctrica. Cada plataforma tardó menos de 12 horas en hacerlo.
Los investigadores hicieron las pruebas en secreto y sin avisar a las empresas. Dos plataformas produjeron planes para fabricar y detonar un artefacto explosivo improvisado en un vehículo. Las otras dos, para atacar subestaciones eléctricas, una con un dron y otra con armas de fuego.
Las cuatro propusieron un lugar concreto en una gran ciudad de Estados Unidos: un hotel, un centro de convenciones o subestaciones eléctricas. Tres sugirieron cuándo actuar. Dos dieron fechas y horas exactas y otra señaló una estación del año. Según ABC News, las que planeaban explosivos incluyeron consejos para evitar a la policía.
La GAO aclara que la información no era nueva. La diferencia es que las plataformas la reunieron en planes viables en cuestión de horas y no de semanas o meses.
Las protecciones se activaron, pero se esquivaron con la IA
En todos los casos, los pedidos de la GAO activaron las defensas de los chatbots: rechazaron la solicitud, borraron información o suspendieron la cuenta. Los investigadores las sortearon con técnicas comunes para saltarse esas barreras. El informe no detalla las instrucciones ni los métodos, para que nadie pueda repetir la prueba.

articles.title: Quién es Bill Gates y qué está haciendo en la actualidad
articles.summary:
La visita de Bill Gates a la Argentina, registrada en imágenes del barrio porteño de La Boca y del puerto de Ushuaia, disparó la pregunta sobre quién es el hombre detrás de Microsoft y a qué dedica su tiempo en 2026. El cofundador de la compañía de software mantuvo en reserva los motivos de su viaje y no trascendió una agenda oficial, pero su recorrido bastó para poner otra vez en el centro de la escena a uno de los empresarios más influyentes del mundo.
Hoy, Gates ya no dirige Microsoft ni concentra su actividad pública en el desarrollo de software. Su trabajo actual está repartido entre la filantropía orientada a la salud global, la inversión en IA aplicada a países en desarrollo y el financiamiento de tecnologías para descarbonizar la economía, todo bajo la estructura de su fundación y de su fondo de inversión climática.
Quién es Bill Gates
Bill Gates nació en 1955 en Seattle, en una familia donde la educación y la disciplina ocupaban un lugar central. Su padre, William H. Gates Sr., era abogado, y su madre, Mary Maxwell Gates, tuvo una trayectoria destacada en el ámbito empresarial y filantrópico.
Ese entorno marcó su formación desde temprano. En su libro de memorias Source Code: My Beginnings, primero de una trilogía centrada en sus años previos a la fundación de Microsoft, Gates recuerda que su abuela materna le enseñó a jugar a las cartas, una actividad que despertó en él un interés temprano por los sistemas de datos y la estrategia.
